events.title: Let the Poets Speak: A Celebration of Philip Glass + Allen Ginsberg
events.description:
Stanford Live Presents
Let the Poets Speak: A Celebration of Philip Glass and Allen Ginsberg
Featuring Timo Andres, Taylor Mac, & the San Francisco Girls Chorus

Friday, October 30 | Bing Concert Hall

On the occasion of composer Philip Glass’s 90th birthday, Let the Poets Speak celebrates Glass’s extraordinary relationships and collaborations with poets. Throughout his long career, Glass has drawn inspiration from poets’ words, lives, and the depths of their creative practice. Poetry has played a key role in the evolution of his music—from Rumi to Leonard Cohen—and, in particular, with one of Glass's closest friends and collaborators: American beat poet Allen Ginsberg, who posthumously celebrates his own centennial in 2026. For this program, Philip Glass composed original works for Allen Ginsberg’s poems including “Wichita Vortex Sutra” and “Magic Psalm”.

Featuring performances by longtime Glass interpreter pianist Timo Andres, theater artist Taylor Mac, poet and filmmaker Chinaka Hodge, poet and Stanford lecturer in the ITALIC Sam Sax, and members of the San Francisco Girls Chorus, this evening celebrates not only these seminal American cultural icons, but the spirit of collaboration across generations.

Note: Philip Glass will not be performing.

This performance may contain sexual themes and sensitive topics. Recommended for ages 16 and up.

Co-commissioned by Pomegranate Arts and UCSB Arts and Lectures.

events.title: Love, Loss, and Letting Go
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Vinny Ferraro and Frank Ostaseski
There is no getting through a human life without loss. The question is not whether we will be asked to let go, but how we will meet what must be let go. In this half-day, we’ll explore how practice can help us meet grief, love, and impermanence without turning away. Together we’ll reflect on how to meet both the suffering of the world and the more intimate losses of our own lives with honesty, care, and courage.
This is not about transcending grief or arriving at some perfected acceptance. It’s about what helps us stay open, present, and human when life asks us to let go.
Join us to reflect more deeply on letting go and on appreciating the life that is here now.

She hoped to start her own nonprofit, hire a crew, and distribute more meals, which led her to make her first batch of guava-filled coyotas (a style of pastry from Sonora, Mexico) as a fundraiser. events.title: Halloween (1978)
events.description:
In 1978, legendary New Yorker film critic Pauline Kael reviewed John Carpenter's HALLOWEEN. She didn’t like it.

"HALLOWEEN has a pitiful, amateurish script (by Carpenter and his producer, Debra Hill). An escaped lunatic wielding a kitchen knife stalks people in a small Midwestern town (Haddonfield, Illinois), and that's about it. Maybe when a horror film is stripped of everything but dumb scariness – when it isn't ashamed to revive the stalest device of the genre (the escaped lunatic) – it satisfies part of the audience in a more basic, childish way than sophisticated horror pictures do."

Eternal respect to Ms. Kael, but what she disdained more than 40 years ago are the very elements that have made this film endure for over four decades.

HALLOWEEN might not have resembled the “sophisticated” horror films of the 1970s, but the simplicity of the film’s story and production values allowed Carpenter to focus on staying one step ahead of the audience. From Dean Cundey's flowing, blue-hued photography to Carpenter's minimalist score to the blank, ominous mask of Michael Myers, nothing in this moody, terrifying film is misplaced.

Just as BLAZING SADDLES, DIE HARD, and THE MATRIX reinvigorated their genres by satisfying in “basic, childish ways,” Carpenter created a pitch-perfect prototype in HALLOWEEN that changed an entire genre forever.

Simon Posford is a pioneering force in psychedelic electronic music, shaping generations of artists through his groundbreaking work as Hallucinogen and SHPONGLE. His early releases Twisted and The Lone Deranger helped define the global psytrance movement, while SHPONGLE reimagined electronic music into a genre-defying fusion of ambient, world, and psychedelic sound.

Today, SHPONGLE (Simon Posford Live) is a rare, fully immersive experience—blending live instrumentation, cutting-edge production, and deep improvisation. Described as the “Psychedelic Olympics,” his performances push the boundaries of music and sensory experience.

His 2025 tour sold out across every city, including multi-night runs in New York, Denver, and San Francisco.

A true pioneer, Posford continues to redefine what live electronic music can be.

Wake the Dead, The Bay Area's own Celtic All-Star Summer of Love party band, is returning to the Freight for their 26th annual Day of the Dead Bash, always the sell-out party of the season! THE GYMNASTS OF FISHERMAN COLONY is an intimate coming-of-age documentary by 3X Emmy Award-winning filmmaker Habiba Nosheen that follows three teenage girls in Pakistan, offering a rare and tender portrait of girlhood, joy, and play told through the eyes of young Pakistani girls navigating the margins of society.

At its core, THE GYMNASTS OF FISHERMAN COLONY is a story of hope and quiet defiance. Through the intimate journeys of three teenagers we witness as their passion for gymnastics begins to clash with deeply rooted expectations around what girls can and cannot do. The film follows their journey as they find themselves straddling two polar opposite worlds as they push to make space for themselves through gymnastics. The result is a lyrical and deeply human portrait of three young girls from a corner of the world we rarely see on screen.

These are girls who dare to dream.

events.title: Wreckless Strangers Live in Sausalito
events.description:
Wreckless Strangers is a collective of friends and musicians carrying the torch for San Francisco’s grand rock ‘n’ roll tradition. Their unique blend of “Ameri-Cali Soul” melds the contemporary blues stylings of Bonnie Raitt and Boz Scaggs; the songwriting sensibilities of Sons of Champlin and Fleetwood Mac; the swashbuckling Americana of the Lost Planet Airmen and Peter Rowan; and the funk of Sly Stone and Tower of Power with a dash of Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane for flavor and unpredictability. With soaring vocal harmonies and burning instrumental improvisation, framed by concise, poignant original songwriting, Wreckless Strangers seek to honor and carry forth the brand of free-spirited musical fun and adventure that defines the Bay Area.

The band features Amber Morris on lead vocals; David Noble on lead guitar and lead vocals; Joshua Zucker on bass and vocals; Mick Hellman on drums and vocals; Rob Anderson on guitar and vocals; and Fletcher Nielsen on keys.
Dirty Souls is the band’s third studio outing under the tutelage of Grammy-winning producer Dave Way, who fosters a level of depth and organic cohesion that firmly establishes Wreckless Strangers in San Francisco’s storied rock ’n’ roll legacy. The songwriting is among their most intimate and personal, exploring themes of relationships, loss, empowerment, and perseverance. events.title: Plant Wisdom for Day of the Dead: Acacia Confusa + Syrian Rue
events.description: Some plants come with thousands of years of stories attached. In this two-hour workshop, Jennifer Langford explores Acacia confusa and Syrian rue, two plants with long histories of ceremonial and ancestral use. You'll learn where they come from, how different cultures have understood and worked with them, and the traditions that have gathered around them over time. Held on Day of the Dead, it's a fitting moment to think about memory, lineage, and how plant knowledge gets handed from one generation to the next. The afternoon closes with a non-psychedelic tea offering and a guided Yoga Nidra practice, so you'll leave both smarter and deeply relaxed. To skip the ticket fees, register in person at the Church of Mother Gong.

events.title: Organ Recital: English and American Masterworks
events.description:
Dr. Justin Murphy-Mancini from Pacific Lutheran University will offer a pipe-organ recital on "English and American Masterworks" on the 1924 E. M. Skinner organ in the sublime acoustics of Trinity St. Peter's. The program features hidden gems written in the last 150 years. Prominent American composers of yesteryear, like Henry Dunham, are contrasted with major figures of the 20th century, including Emma Lou Diemer, Undine Smith Moore, and Miriam Gideon. These are paired with works by composers across the pond, including Kenneth Leighton and Samuel Coleridge-Taylor. The crown jewel is Herbert Howells's Master Tallis' Testament. This concert has a little of everything, from Bachian inspired fireworks, to dense chromaticism, to unadulterated joy. It is a diverse, yet coherent musical experience.

Free

Presented by Palo Alto/Peninsula Chapter of the American Guild of Organists

events.title: The Musical Box
events.description:
Renowned for their high quality reproductions of historic Genesis performances since 1993, The Musical Box takes fans along for a time-travel ride, offering people a chance to relive the magic of this unique experience.

These replicas has required exhaustive visual, scenic, audio and musical research even tracking down the original music instruments used at the time. The visual aspect of The Musical Box shows are based on thousands of photos and many amateur films taken at the Genesis concerts, as well as the original slides used by the group during their shows.

Impressively, The Musical Box is the only group licensed and supported by Genesis and Peter Gabriel and has presented close to 1000 concerts across the world to more than one million spectators, in prestigious amphitheaters such as The Royal Albert Hall in London, the Olympia in Paris and the Bell Center in Montreal.

Peter Gabriel, who saw the concert was ”really impressed by the production quality and the attention to detail”; Steve Hackett and Phil Collins have even joined The Musical Box on stage.

''The Musical Box play it better than we did'' stated Phil Collins after seeing The Musical Box's production in Geneva.

A Musical Box show is a unique opportunity to discover the mystical Genesis concerts and to relive a historic rock moment.

events.title: Club Kid, in 35mm
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment and SFFILM present
Club Kid (in 35mm)
Monday, November 2 | The Castro

Club Kid plunges audiences headfirst into the exhilarating, sybaritic universe of New York City nightlife. First-time writer-director Jordan Firstman stars as Peter, a magnetic club promoter whose lifestyle of revelry is upended when he unexpectedly discovers he fathered a young boy. Thrust into parenthood, Peter navigates his newfound responsibilities in fits and starts, relying heavily on his chosen family as he works to establish a philosophy for intimate love. Firstman’s script and performance deftly balance outrageous humor and anarchic energy with an unexpected emotional generosity. Newcomer Reggie Absolom is terrific as Peter’s son, Arlo, holding his own alongside a wonderfully unpredictable ensemble featuring Cara Delevingne, Diego Calva, Kirby Howell-Baptiste, Miss Benny, and Colleen Camp. Presented in 35mm, the film possesses a tactile physicality and vivid sense of place, while killer needle drops perfectly compliment the multitudes of Peter and Arlo’s experiences. Poignant and irreverent, Club Kid offers an insider’s glimpse into a distinctive culture while resonating with anyone who has struggled to find their place in the world. Funny, heartfelt, and singular, Club Kid is an irresistible invitation to experience something you won’t soon forget. —Jessie Fairbanks

"Fernando, a Peruvian single father, sits in an audio-recording room with his young son Dylan, recording voices together from Spanish into Quechua their indigenous language. Fernando provides careful but spirited direction to Dylan, who nails the specific intonation. What seems as a playful game between a father and son is actually a treasured creative hobby for Fernando, who has dubbed online clips of many animated movies into Quechua. As a voice actor whos always had an interest in crafting voices and dialects, Fernando uses his platform as a radio host in his native Cusco to create content in Quechua, enabling this language to thrive and not be forgotten. Our language Quechua, affirms Fernando, is like life itself.

NAZA is also playing at NEW PEOPLE

In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

Directors Note:

We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanisation of another?

What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

– Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

events.title: Marjorie Keller: Intimate Observer
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 6:30pm / Film 7pm

$15 / free or discounted for members

Marjorie Keller was one of the most significant figures in late 20th century American experimental film. A profoundly original artist, scholar, teacher and advocate, Keller was staunchly feminist without limiting herself to that movement’s ideological orthodoxies. Fiercely independent, her work was sharply critical of the customary role women were relegated to in patriarchal society, even as she embraced aspects of traditional family life. Keller cherished the mostly male history of avant-garde filmmaking, but she was one of the foremost advocates for women film artists throughout her life. When she died at age 43 in 1994, Keller had already produced twenty-seven 8mm and 16mm films. They were remarkable for their thematic and poetical complexity and by investigating her domestic life as a woman for their starting point. Her expressive cinematography and intricate montage were sensual, emotional and intellectually challenging, and while she was clearly influenced by such predecessors as Marie Menken, Stan Brakhage and Saul Levine, Keller's cinematic voice was distinctly her own from beginning with her first film.

In conjunction with the publication of a new book on Keller's work, In the Absence of Marjorie Keller, edited by Robin Blaetz and Scott Hammen, two programs of her films, spanning twenty-four years, will be presented by Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive and San Francisco Cinematheq...

Please join the GLBT Historical Society and Crowded Fire Theater as we jointly present the first of two staged readings of How to Live in a House on Fire, a new play by Kari Barclay and directed by M. Graham Smith.

Presented for the first time in the San Francisco Bay Area where the story takes place, this staged reading of a new play by performance scholar Kari Barclay looks to queer history as a lens to understand our current moment of climate grief.

By 1989 acclaimed Scottish actor Ian Charleson (a sensational Andrew Scott, All of Us Strangers), who had career-defining roles in Oscar-winning pictures Chariots of Fire (1981) and Gandhi (1982), yearns for his next great role. For Charleson, a gay man with AIDS, navigating Hollywood and keeping his personal life private is a minefield, and he’s drawn to the idea of revisiting his stage-actor roots. When Daniel Day Lewis abandons Richard Eyre’s (Johnny Flynn, Ripley) production of Hamlet at the National Theatre mid-performance, Charleson is poised to take over the play’s title role.

But the actor’s ambitious return is halted when he develops Kaposi’s sarcoma, prompting his doctor (Oscar winner Olivia Colman, The Favourite) to forbid him from taking on such a strenuous role. Featuring memorable supporting turns from Joe Locke(Heartstopper) and David Dawson (My Policeman), who plays renowned queer filmmaker Derek Jarman, Simon Stone’s latest is a deeply resonant film about the power of art and human connection in the face of mortality, all moored by a career-best, Oscar-worthy performance from Scott.

events.description:
Join us to savor the poetry of the season, in this free gathering hosted by Jayne McPherson.

Gardens have an essential and ubiquitous place in lyric poetry. The great poet Kahlil Gibran called friendship a garden, one where planted seeds are sown "with love and reap thanksgiving."

During this season, let's follow his poetic lead and look up at distant mountains that frame the lazy lady on the horizon. Let's remind ourselves of the middle pond's pink and white lotus blossoms-that they float night and day under the sun or moonlight. Let's notice how the water fountain's splash undulates in ringlets; how, inside the iron gate, blossoms protrude as promises kept in heirloom roses; how a giving-tree oak allows another woodpecker or squirrel to sneak substance and nest.

Haiku offers beauty in form and empathy. And like a harvest, it can evoke awe or perhaps simply ahhh. When we seek pause in the natural world, we may remember our breath and breathe more deeply. We may tune in, feel our heartbeat, sense a door opening as we pause before a sunning lizard or grazing deer.

Writing haiku is a quiet way to savor these Garden gifts.

This is our third anniversary writing circle and will feature haikuist, David Watts. His poetry has been published widely. It includes two books, Dream Tree & Seed Kites.

David Watts is recognized by Haiku Poets of Northern California.

Studio 8 Film Festival presents:
Where to? (Juror Night)

This year's open call jurors show their own work: Nine Years Behind the Wheel (Ed Jones, 1986), Lullaby To My Father and Lullaby To My Father: Redux (Michael LaRocco, 2019), and Lost or Found (Jacalyn White and Joell Hallowell, 2020).

Shot from the driver's seat of his night-shift cab, Ed Jones's Nine Years Behind the Wheel is a diary of San Francisco in the '80s and of an artist trying to keep going. Passengers, SFAI openings, No Nothing Cinema at 30 Berry Street, a young Mike Henderson, Marian Wallace, Michael Rudnick, family, friends, bands: all of it filmed between fares, with wit and a great soundtrack.

In Lullaby To My Father and its Redux, Michael LaRocco revisits his father's absence after discovering that his father had a second family in Vietnam during the war.

Lost or Found gathers phone footage from friends and family across 21st-century American life, leading into the 2020 shelter-in-place, and remixes it into improbable, often funny juxtapositions.

Screening will be followed by a conversation with all three jurors, moderated by V. Vale of RE/Search.

events.title: Robert Shields: My Life as a Robot
events.description:
Robert Shields: My Life as a Robot celebrates the extraordinary, and often invisible, impact one artist can have on the world. In the 1970s, Robert Shields began performing his signature robot routine outside the Hollywood Wax Museum before later moving to street performances in San Francisco’s Union Square. Within a few short years, he and his wife, Lorene Yarnell, were headlining their own hit CBS variety series, The Shields & Yarnell Show. What Robert didn’t fully realize at the time was that his robot would go on to influence the DNA of popping, locking, and hip-hop dance as we know it today.

Funny, joyful, and full of genuine wonder, the film introduces you to a man who makes you believe anything is possible — including, as Robert demonstrates, street skiing through downtown San Francisco.

Followed by a live performance by Poppin John; a Q&A with Robert Shields, director Mark Bonn, producer Christine Seibert Bonn, and Poppin John, moderated by Peter L. Stein; and a post-screening reception in the lobby.

Info and tickets: https://sfdancefilmfest.org/fall-festival-2026/robert-shields/

events.description:
Wendy Clarke, Inside Out (still), 2002

Doors 6pm / Screening 6:30pm

Free

A screening and conversation with Wendy Clarke and Nigel Poor, presented in collaboration with Cushion Works and Ear Hustle on the occasion of the exhibition Wendy Clarke: The Prison Tapes on view through Nov. 14, 2026.

Wendy Clarke is a video pioneer whose practice spans more than five decades. The daughter of avant-garde filmmaker Shirley Clarke, she has spent her career positioning the camera as a tool for intimacy, dialogue, and human connection across social and institutional boundaries. She is best known for Love Tapes, a collection of over 2,500 video recordings of people talking about love.

In conjunction with The Prison Tapes (1979-2002), an exhibition on view at Cushion Works through November 14, The Lab presents an evening with Clarke. The program includes a screening of rarely-seen video work and a discussion with the artist Nigel Poor, co-founder and co-host of Ear Hustle, the first podcast created and produced inside a prison. Their conversation will be recorded and presented as a special episode of the podcast.

For several years in the 1980s and 90s, Clarke was an artist in residence within the California prison system—at the Ventura Youth Correctional Facility, the California Institution for Men in Chino, and the CIM Del Norte facility, working primarily with men in the HIV/AIDS unit. In dingy dayrooms and with minimal resources, she created the conditions for exchange and discovery...

events.title: Rituals of Care: Buddhist Chant and Culture
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Chenxing Han and Trent Walker
What is the role of chant in Buddhist practice? How does it shape communities of belonging and cultures of care?
During this daylong, we will engage in a variety of chanting practices from across the Buddhist world, with a special emphasis on the Theravāda tradition as transmitted in mainland Southeast Asia. We’ll explore the musical and textual dimensions of chant, as well as its ritual possibilities. Our charge as a group will be to embody chant as an expression of care for ourselves, our loved ones, and the world.
There will be time to reflect on questions of voice, language, and lineage. Nearly every Buddhist throughout history has engaged in recitation and other practices of aspiration, concentration, and devotion. Our day together invites us into kinship with them as we, too, experience the healing resonances of these practices.
All are warmly welcome to participate; no previous chanting experience is required.

events.title: Two Films. One Manilatown Legacy.
events.description:
"Two Films. One Manilatown Legacy." brings two generations of San Francisco's Manilatown and International Hotel history to the big screen at SFMOMA for a special FREE double-feature presentation.

At 1 PM, experience the San Francisco premiere of the newly enhanced and restored edition of Curtis Choy's landmark 1983 documentary, "The Fall of the I-Hotel". The film chronicles the decade-long struggle to save San Francisco's International Hotel and the August 4, 1977 eviction of its predominantly Filipino and Chinese elder tenants. Following the screening, filmmaker Curtis Choy joins co-producers of the enhanced edition for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.

At 3 PM, experience the premiere of "Manilatown Manang", the story of Jeanette Gandionco Lazam-artist, activist, and one of the few women who lived in the International Hotel as a Tenant Defender during the historic anti-eviction movement. The film follows Jeanette's journey from the I-Hotel struggle through a lifetime of activism, art, and community. Following the premiere, Jeanette Lazam joins the film's producers and creative team for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.

Together, the films create a powerful dialogue between past and present: audiences first encounter Jeanette as a young activist in Choy's historic documentary, then experience the continuation of her story in Manilatown Manang.

events.title: Kolam: At the Threshold
events.address: 1700 Alum Rock Avenue, San Jose, CA, 95116
events.description:
Abhinaya Dance Company, an Indian classical dance company founded by Artistic Director Mythili Kumar announces Kolam: At the Threshold* on Saturday, November 7, 4 pm at the Mexican Heritage Plaza in San Jose.

Kolam: At the Threshold, choreographed by Abhinaya Principal Artist and Choreographer Rasika Kumar, is a new full-length 80-minute Bharatanatyam dance work that explores ritual, inheritance, and cultural memory through the South Indian practice of kolam-daily rice-flour drawings made at the threshold of the home. The piece integrates Bharatanatyam movement, Carnatic music, spoken text, and spatial design inspired by kolam's geometric structures.

Kolam centers the threshold as both a physical and symbolic space-between inside and outside, tradition and modernity, belonging and exclusion. The artistic vision is to transform the daily ritual of kolam into a contemporary performance structure, using its principles of symmetry, repetition, and impermanence as choreographic tools.

*Kolam: At the Threshold is inspired by the book Feeding a Thousand Souls: Women, Ritual, and Ecology in India- An Exploration of the Kolam, by Vijaya Nagarajan, Associate Professor in the Department of Theology and Religious Studies at the University of San Francisco.

$40-$70.

Presented by Abhinaya Dance Company

events.title: Growing Up on the Hippie Trail: Caleb Dardick at Adobe Books
events.description:
What was it like to grow up in the counterculture — from the back seat of a VW bus?

Join author Caleb Dardick at Adobe Books for a free reading and discussion of his new memoir, The Adventures of Superfreak: My Childhood on the Hippie Trail (Running Wild Press, 2026).

In 1970, five-year-old Caleb traveled from Amsterdam to India with his parents and two younger siblings. His father used a wheelchair, his mother was living with undiagnosed bipolar disorder, and the family embarked on a 20,000-mile adventure through Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and India.

Funny, adventurous, and deeply personal, the memoir explores the counterculture through a child's eyes, capturing both the wonder and instability of an extraordinary family journey.

A longtime Bay Area resident who wrote much of the book in Berkeley, Dardick returns to San Francisco as the city approaches the 60th anniversary of the Summer of Love in 2027.

Lalo Guerrero (1916–2005) was a Mexican-American artist whose restless versatility spanned salsa, norteña, banda, rancheras, boleros, corridos, cumbias, mambos, cha cha chás, swing, rock & roll, and blues. A recipient of the NEA National Heritage Fellowship and the National Medal of Arts, he left a body of work that still echoes across genres and generations.

The Big Star Quintet
Saturday, November 7 | The Fillmore

After many years celebrating the music of Big Star via the collective known as Big Star’s Third, Jody Stephens (the last surviving member of the original Big Star lineup) had an idea.

“I truly loved touring the world and performing Big Star’s Third with a core group, a variety of special guests, and a chamber orchestra playing the beautiful orchestrations created by Carl Marsh and Chris Stamey. But when the idea of celebrating the 50th anniversary of #1 Record came up, it was time to pare the production down to a five-piece rock band. So I called a few close and like-spirited musical friends.”

Enter some of the legendary group’s biggest fans, who have long been associated with Big Star and related projects. The band now includes Mike Mills (R.E.M.), Jon Auer (The Posies), Pat Sansone (Wilco), Chris Stamey (The dB's) and Stephens. Dubbing themselves the Big Star Quintet, it’s a lineup that is both personal and close in spirit to #1 Record and Radio City.

When the newly-minted Quintet gathered at R.E.M.’s rehearsal spot in November of 2022 to commune with the music and workshop as a five-piece for the first time, none of them could have foreseen the rapturous receptions they would receive over the next few years: sold-out shows in the US, playing abroad (including two tours of Spain), both #1 Record and Radio City 50th-anniversary tours, and stellar reviews of their live shows in Uncut, The San Francisco Gate, and bey...

events.description:
with Christopher Germer and Carolina Bautista-Velez
What’s wrong with you? Who do you think you are?
All humans can experience shame—including the most practiced meditators and meditation teachers. It can even happen when we’re entirely innocent of wrongdoing, as well as when we make a mistake. Whenever we feel bad about ourselves, for whatever reason, there’s usually a touch of shame present. It strikes us at the core of our being and yet has nothing to do with who we really are.
The power of shame is largely an illusion. As meditation teacher Tara Brach says, shame often masquerades as a “trance of unworthiness” that gets its power from our instinctive avoidance of it. However, when we look at shame through the eyes of self-compassion, we can discover something quite surprising—that shame is an innocent emotion arising from a universal wish to be loved. This insight opens the door to compassion and self-understanding. Research shows that self-compassion is the opposite of shame. As self-compassion goes up, shame goes down.
In this workshop, Chris Germer and Carolina Bautista-Velez present the practice of Self-Compassion for Shame, specifically tailored to loosen the grip of shame in our own lives. The workshop includes short talks, exercises, practices, and discussion. Participants will learn 5-6 simple tools to bring home to use in their daily life.

WORDS OF LOVE

Sunday, November 8
2:00PM

Marianne & Leonard: Words of Love, renowned filmmaker Nick Broomfield’s documentary chronicles their relationship, from the early days in Greece. Conspiracy of Beards will sing a few songs before the movie starts!

The San Francisco Leonard Cohen Festival presents a screening of Marianne & Leonard: Words of Love, renowned filmmaker Nick Broomfield’s most personal and romantic film of his storied career. The documentary starts on the Greek island of Hydra in 1960, where Leonard Cohen, then a struggling and unknown fiction writer, and Marianne Ihlen, a single mother with a young son, became part of a community of expat artists, writers and musicians. Never-before-seen footage shot by Broomfield and legendary documentarian D.A. Pennebaker makes for a unique portrait of an idyllic 1960’s bohemia. It was a time that left a lasting imprint on both Marianne and Leonard, whose friendship would last another fifty years before their deaths in 2016.

Wajda’s first film where he received sole screenwriting credit, this deeply personal homage to his beloved actor Zbigniew Cybulski, the star of Ashes and Diamonds, is also a scathing portrait of the film industry.

events.venue: Jewish Community Center of San Francisco
events.description:
Join us for the San Francisco premiere of Hold On To Your Music: A Mother's Legacy, including a live performance by internationally acclaimed concert pianist Mona Golabek.

Vienna, 1938. The parents of 14-year-old piano prodigy Lisa Jura faced an unimaginable choice: which of their three daughters to send to safety on the Kindertransport. They chose Lisa. She arrived alone in London, carrying her dreams, memories of her family, and her mother's parting words: "Hold on to your music."

Directed by Academy Award nominated Josh Aronson and Emmy Award winner Adam Wood, the film tells Lisa's remarkable story through rare archival footage, newly restored recordings, and performances by her daughter, Mona Golabek. Drawing on Golabek's best-selling book and acclaimed stage production, The Pianist of Willesden Lane, it celebrates the enduring power of music and a mother's love - a story that has reached more than 20 million people worldwide.

Following the screening and live performance, Golabek joins director Josh Aronson and producer Susan Solomon Libitzky in conversation with executive producer, Dr. Anita Friedman.

events.title: Jeffrey Foucault
events.description:
In two decades on the road Jeffrey Foucault has become one of the most distinctive voices in American music, refining a sound instantly recognizable for its simplicity and emotional power. With a string of critically acclaimed studio albums – “Stark, literate songs that are as wide open as the landscape of his native Midwest” (The New Yorker), "Beat-up troubadour folk whittled to dolorous perfection” (Uncut), “Songwriting Brilliance,” (Irish Times) – he’s built a brick-and-mortar international touring career and a devoted following, one that includes luminaries like Van Dyke Parks, Greil Marcus, and Don Henley.

In September of 2024 Jeffrey Foucault will release The Universal Fire (Fluff & Gravy, 9/6/24), his first album of entirely new material since 2018. A series of high-voltage performances cut live in one room, the album is both a working wake – Foucault lost his best friend and drummer Billy Conway, to cancer in 2021 – and a meditation on the nature of beauty, artifact, and loss.

Augmenting Foucault's all-star band with members of Calexico and Bon Iver (drummer John Convertino and producer/saxophonist Mike Lewis) The Universal Fire sets Conway’s death against the massive 2008 fire at the Universal Studios lot in California that destroyed the master recordings of some of our bedrock American music, to interrogate ideas about mortality, legacy, meaning, and calling.

Canyon at The Roxie is back with a spotlight on local legend Charles Rock Ross! Rock Ross: Go Like This surveys 20 years of the filmmaker’s “frivolous and socially irresponsible films” (The Athens News), bringing together 16mm prints and camera originals from the Academy Film Archive and Canyon Cinema collections.

The longtime Bay Area independent filmmaker, musician, and organizer has been crafting wryly exuberant, riotous work since the early-1970s. After receiving his BFA and MFA in Filmmaking from the San Francisco Art Institute, Ross worked as Film Inspector and Shipper for the Canyon Cinema Co-op from 1975 to 1978, Editing Facility Manager for Film Arts Foundation from 1982 to 1986, and in 1988, served as Director of the Ann Arbor Film Festival. As a founding member and projectionist of the No Nothing Cinema (1982-1997) and New Nothing Cinema (1997-2017), Ross has screened thousands of independent and experimental films and videos. As a title designer, from 1978 to 2013, Ross designed thousands of titles for independent films, shooting directly on film using his own animation stand. He has also scored a number of films with his band, The Goat Family, which formed in 2003.

“Film as art has no bounds… For me its potential is as exciting as pure white noise.” – Rock Ross

events.title: Holy Wave
events.description:
In Ensenada, Mexico, where the Pacific horizon cuts a clean, unwavering line, Holy Wave recorded their latest full length, i’m DADA, a record that feels both expansive and newly concentrated for the subterranean pop four-piece. Stepping outside the United States was less a retreat than a shift in perspective, creating distance to recognize a new sound that had been slowly taking shape among them. i’m DADA quickly revealed its character: more propulsive, more candid, and their most structurally deliberate work to date.

Working alongside experimental duo Lorelle Meets the Obsolete at their studio El Derrumbe the sessions folded community into the album, though its emotional core had already formed over months of pre-production. Half of Holy Wave is Mexican, with roots in the El Paso border region, so recording in Ensenada felt intuitive and relaxed. Joo Joo Ashworth, mixing engineer and longtime friend, also provided a pivotal presence helping crystallize the album’s rhythmic language and subtly expanding the band’s sound. The songs began reflecting conversations about fatherhood and partnership, breakups and estrangement, the queasy acceleration of AI, and what it means to remain present and principled while the world lurches unpredictably forward.

Presented by Kilowatt.

This is a 21+ event

events.title: Brand New
events.description: Formed in 2000 on Long Island, New York, Brand New is an American alternative rock band consisting of Jesse Lacey, Vincent Accardi, Garrett Tierney, and Brian Lane. After signing with Triple Crown Records, the band released their debut album, Your Favorite Weapon, in 2001, establishing themselves within the Long Island emo and pop-punk scene. Their breakthrough second album, Deja Entendu, arrived in 2003 and featured the singles “The Quiet Things That No One Ever Knows” and “Sic Transit Gloria Glory Fades.” The album showcased a more mature sound and was later certified Gold in the United States. Following a major-label bidding war, the band signed with DreamWorks/Interscope and released The Devil and God Are Raging Inside Me in 2006, a record that would become one of the most influential albums of the emo era. In 2009, they put out their fourth album Daisy, reaching No. 6 on the Billboard 200. Brand New returned in 2017 with Science Fiction, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and received widespread critical acclaim.

In the United Kingdom, they had ten Top 40 hits including "Tainted Love" (#1 UK), "Torch" (#2 UK), "Say Hello, Wave Goodbye" (#3 UK), "What!" (#3 UK), and "Bedsitter" (#4 UK), and also had four Top 20 albums between 1981 and 1984. In 1984, the duo split but reformed in 2001 to tour and record new material, releasing their fifth studio album, Cruelty Without Beauty in 2002.

Soft Cell's songs have been covered by various artists including Nine Inch Nails, David Gray, Nouvelle Vague, and A-ha.[citation needed] Their track, "Memorabilia", earned recognition for the band as pioneers of the synth-oriented techno genre. The duo have sold 10 million records worldwide.

The La Pipa de la Paz 30th Anniversary Tour continues across the Americas and Europe, celebrating one of Latin rock's most iconic records. events.title: You're Just a Thing: The Art of Objectification with Miss Red Rida
events.description:
Class: 7–9:30pm · Play: 9:30–10:30pm · $75/couple · $40/single

A footstool. A coat rack. A pretty little decoration. Why is it so hot to be reduced to a thing, and so satisfying to treat someone like one?

Miss Red Rida and her sub Sparrow Lark come from both sides of the D/s dynamic, and they'll show you how to do it well. You'll explore what pulls tops and bottoms toward objectification, try out its many flavors and styles, and learn how it's different from degradation and humiliation.

Come ready to be furniture, or to furnish your space with a willing body. You might be the chair someone sinks into, the table that holds their drink perfectly still, the lamp that glows on command, or the hook they hang their keys on when they walk through the door. Or you might be the one choosing where your thing goes and how long it stays there.

You'll brainstorm objectifying words and try them out on each other, get into human furniture positions, and play games that turn people into props. The class ends with an hour of open play where you can put your thing to use!

The exercises are made for pairs, and solo observers are welcome.

What to wear: Whatever feels comfy and sexy to you. The class involves some basic movement.

Ólafur Arnalds
Thursday, November 12 | The Castro

Award-winning artist, composer and producer Ólafur Arnalds returns with his most daring and adventurous project to date.

Falling Apart Together is an attempt at dismantling the distance between us. A concert hybrid that reveals the layers we construct in order to feel safe, the moments in which those layers tremble and the sense of intimacy and shared humanity that emerges when we allow ourselves to be exposed.

Together with his team of devoted craftsmen and musicians, Ólafur presents a spellbinding blend of past and new material in a show that challenges the boundaries of what a concert can be.

After his globally acclaimed tours following re:member and some kind of peace — which sold out such iconic halls as Royal Albert Hall, Elbphilharmonie, Sydney Opera House, and Walt Disney Concert Hall – performing to hundreds of thousands of fans worldwide — Ólafur returns with his most intimate and boundary-pushing work to date.

Falling Apart Together explores what becomes possible when we let ourselves unravel just enough to collectively open up.

events.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
events.description:
Even in his darkest films, Pedro Almodóvar never shies away from peppering whimsy and fun into his explorations of the fringes of the human psyche. With his 1988 classic WOMEN ON THE VERGE OF A NERVOUS BREAKDOWN, he delightfully flips that equation, resulting in a hugely funny and whimsical film that lightly peppers human insight throughout.

Actress Pepa Marcos (Carmen Maura, MATADOR) is, well, on the verge of a nervous breakdown. Having been abandoned by her lover, she embarks on a quest to reestablish contact with him, all the while navigating the stresses of live animals, answering machines, apartment fires, a girlfriend with accidental ties to terrorism, her ex-lover’s son (Antonio Banderas, PAIN AND GLORY), sleeping pills, and inquisitive detectives.

With his trademark color palette, dynamic camerawork, and a virtuoso performance from Carmen Maura in the lead role, WOMEN ON THE VERGE OF A NERVOUS BREAKDOWN takes the pain of heartbreak and wrings every last laugh out of it.

events.description:
Tuba Skinny

Thursday, November 12 | The Freight

For over a decade Tuba Skinny has grown steadily in popularity, releasing twelve albums and touring all over the world. They’ve attracted a wide variety of fans, young and old, neophytes and niche-enthusiasts, with the strength of their musicianship and the scope of their jazz and American roots music catalog. The band is composed of Shaye Cohn (cornet), Barnabus Jones (trombone), Todd Burdick (tuba), Craig Flory (clarinet), Gregory Sherman (guitar and vocals), Max Bien-Kahn (banjo), Robin Rapuzzi (washboard), and Erika Lewis (vocals and bass drum).

While they’ve become known as world-class interpreters of traditional jazz, over the years they’ve branched out into jug band music, spirituals, country blues, string band music, ragtime, and New Orleans R&B. Their approach is a true reflection of Americana, encompassing the full genealogy of popular American music from an early 20th century perspective.

No matter how well known they’ve become or how high profile their gigs have gotten, Tuba Skinny has always returned to the streets. “We continue to play in the street because it’s a public space,” says Shaye. “We get to play for everyone: old, young, rich, poor, people from all walks of life. It keeps things interesting because it’s organic and unpredictable.”

School Fair (Findlay Buchanan, Semisi Ma’ia’i, Hamish Morgan, De Stevens and Rose Pickernell) make music embedded in the human experience. It’s a product of the band’s native New Zealand, a place that remains intimate and remote, where emotion is magnified over both distance and familiarity. The five band members began the project renting out a factory-sized, sub-zero degree Celsius room normally operated by construction workers in the industrial area of Ōtepoti, Dunedin, New Zealand in 2021, recording music on the 4-track tape recorder that would become debut Gorse on a Hill. The album remained the only trace of the band online for a few years, an artifact for those who know where to look. School Fair’s music has this sense of self-discovery when you find it, a sound that feels both recognizable and like the vacant expanse of a country whirring by on a train. Still with little to no self-promotion, the appearance of sophomore effort Bird the Kid online in early 2025 was a new portal to their world of melodic and intricate indie music that retains a kind of atmospheric beauty.

Unexpected Violence (Mutual, 2026) is the first record made between geographical places, with the band now split in between London and New Zealand. You can hear this fragmented approach in the patchwork quality and inherent connective tissue of the album. Weaving together chamber classical, folk, torch song, and experimental music, Dorian Wood’s Canto de Todes is a 70-minute distillation born from Wood’s acclaimed 12-hour composition and installation. The title—Spanish for “Song of Everyone”—is inspired by a lyric of the late Chilean singer and songwriter Violeta Parra. Canto de Todes emphasizes the urgency of music as a vessel for social change, and honors the ancestral trajectory of Wood’s Costa Rican-Nicaraguan family and their experience in the U.S.

Dorian Wood (b. 1975, pronouns: she/her/they/them) is an anti-disciplinary artist based in the U.S., whose practice seeks to “infect” spaces and ideologies in order to challenge traditions and systems of marginalization. Her performances, films and visual works have been presented worldwide. From 2019–2020, Wood toured internationally with XAVELA LUX AETERNA, a chamber orchestra tribute to Chavela Vargas. Subsequent works Mares Ocultos (2022), a compositional series centering on deconstructing male heterosexuality.

Born in San Juan, Puerto Rico, Roco Córdova is a vocalist, composer, producer and improviser based in the San Francisco Bay Area. events.title: The Moth GrandSLAM Championship
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
The Moth GrandSLAM Championship

Friday, November 13 | The Castro

The Moth is dedicated to finding people from all walks of life to tell inspired stories. At The Moth StorySLAM, those people find us. On this night, winners from our StorySLAM series compete to determine The San Francisco GrandSLAM Story Champion.

The Moth GrandSLAM is the ultimate storytelling championship, inviting winners from The Moth’s open-mic StorySLAMs back to the stage to battle for the crown. With a full slate of local storytelling pros, you know this night is going to be good. Come experience fierce, hilarious, and sometimes even heartbreaking stories at the Moth GrandSLAM live.

The Moth is a global storytelling nonprofit with the mission to inspire people to listen and share openly, think and feel deeply, and expand their understanding of one another. Since 1997, The Moth has presented more than 70,000 true stories—told live and without notes—in 11 countries, across 4 continents. Today, The Moth produces 600+ live shows annually, as well as the Peabody Award-winning The Moth Radio Hour, and the popular The Moth Podcast. Through workshops for students, educators, adults, advocates, and professionals, The Moth guides thousands of new storytellers each year in finding and sharing their own voices. Learn more at themoth.org @MothStories

events.title: Isaiah Rashad
events.description:
It’s Been Awful marks the moment Isaiah Rashad fully becomes his own genre. The Top Dawg Entertainment visionary returns with his third studio album on May 1, expanding his sonic world beyond hip-hop into cosmic jazz, psychedelic guitar rock, Soulquarian neo-soul, and flashes of genre-blurring experimentation. After five transformative years, Rashad delivers his most vulnerable and fully-realized work yet — an unfiltered reflection on addiction, growth, self-confrontation, and redemption. It’s soul music in its most metaphysical form, anchored by the same lyrical precision and emotional depth that have defined his artistry from the beginning.

Since emerging from Chattanooga, TN in 2012, Rashad has built one of the most impactful and emotionally resonant catalogs in modern rap. His debut Cilvia Demo immediately established him as a critical force, followed by The Sun’s Tirade, which debuted in the Top 20 of the Billboard 200 and earned Gold certification. His 2021 album The House Is Burning further solidified his cultural imprint, amassing nearly one billion global streams and widespread acclaim for its introspective storytelling and sonic evolution. Across his career, Rashad has achieved multiple Gold and Platinum certifications, with standout records including “Wat’s Wrong” (feat. Kendrick Lamar & Zacari) and “Pretty Little Birds” (feat. SZA), while maintaining a loyal, cult-like fanbase drawn to his honesty and depth.

events.title: The Addams Family Musical
events.description:
The Addams Family Musical

In the upside-down world of the Addams Family, to be sad is to be happy, to feel pain is to feel joy, and death and suffering are the stuff of their dreams. Nonetheless, this quirky family still must deal with many of the same challenges faced by any other family, especially now that the Addams kids are getting older.

Wednesday Addams, the beloved princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet young man from a seemingly ordinary family. A man her parents have never met. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host dinner for Wednesday’s boyfriend and his parents.

Full of quirky characters, wicked humor, catchy songs, and plenty of heart, this ghoulishly fun musical is a celebration of family, love, and embracing what makes us different.

events.title: All About My Mother
events.description:
Presented in Spanish with English subtitles

Though Pedro Almodóvar’s films have pushed the boundaries of cinema as far back as the mid-1970s, it wasn’t until 1999’s ALL ABOUT MY MOTHER that the Academy Awards finally took notice, naming it the Best Foreign Language Film of the year. And it serves as a perfect encapsulation of his enduring power as an artist: it’s colorful, dynamic, emotional, darkly funny, and imbued with profound empathy.

When tragedy strikes, Manuela (Cecilia Roth, PEPI, LUCI, BOM) travels to Barcelona for the first time in years in search of someone from her past. But she is waylaid by her old friend Agrado (Antonia San Juan), a transgender sex worker, as well as new friends, such as Hermana (Penélope Cruz, PAIN AND GLORY), a nun with a secret, and Huma (Marisa Paredes, THE SKIN I LIVE IN), an actress performing in town. Together, the women form a unique bond that carries them through the challenges that life throws at them.

Driven by the powerhouse performances of each actress in the film, ALL ABOUT MY MOTHER showcases the humanity of these women at their best and worst, their highest and lowest, resulting in a portrait of friendship, family, and love that is singularly Almodóvar.

Jo Koy is one of today’s premier stand-up comedians, rising from performing in a Las Vegas coffee house to selling out arenas worldwide. His relatable comedy, drawn from his colorful family and Filipino heritage, has connected with audiences across cultures, making him one of the top 10 grossing stand-up comedians each year according to Pollstar and Billboard. He continues selling out and breaking records at prestigious venues around the world.

In 2023, Koy inked a two-special deal with Netflix, with the first special released in 2024. Jo Koy: Live From Brooklyn, filmed at the historic King’s Theatre, premiered globally on June 4 and was the #6 most viewed special that year, with over 240 million minutes watched. He recently filmed his upcoming Netflix special in Stockton, CA, set to release later this year. His other Netflix specials include Live From The Los Angeles Forum, Comin’ In Hot, and Live From Seattle. He also released the variety special Jo Koy: In His Elements, spotlighting Filipino-American culture in Manila. Overall, Koy has had seven highly rated specials across Comedy Central and Netflix.

Koy starred in the 2022 Universal Pictures comedy Easter Sunday, inspired by his life and Filipino roots, produced by Steven Spielberg’s Amblin Partners. He has also appeared in Disney’s Haunted Mansion, voiced characters in Netflix’s Monkey King and Leo, and most recently in Paramount+’s The Tiger’s Apprentic...

events.title: Kino
events.description: Born in the underground clubs of Leningrad in 1981, KINO became the defining voice of Soviet rock — a band that smuggled freedom into every chord when freedom itself was contraband. Fronted by the magnetic Viktor Tsoi, they played to 62,000 at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium in 1990. Months later, Tsoi was gone. The music never stopped. "What Elvis Presley was to America, Tsoi was to Russia." Now, original members Yuri Kasparyan, Alexander Titov, and Igor Tikhomirov bring KINO back to the stage — accompanied by Tsoi's own voice, restored and digitized from original multi-track recordings. This is not a tribute act. This is KINO, continuing the conversation. Expect anthems you know by heart — Gruppa Krovi, Peremen, Posledniy Geroy — performed with the raw urgency that made them timeless. Sung in Russian. Felt in every language.

events.title: Max Jaffe: You Want That Too! + Burden of Dreams
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 8pm / Show 8:30pm

$23 / free or discounted for members

In a trio formation with some of the core rhythm section players from the record, Max Jaffe, Gavin Gamboa, and Logan Kane reimagine the music from Jaffe's 2025 release You Want That Too!

Max Jaffe is a drummer, producer, composer, and technologist based in Los Angeles, CA. His work expands the possibilities of composition and collaboration through the drum set.

In 2025, Jaffe released "You Want That Too!" on Colorfield Records. Eclectic and tuneful, the album received praise from Pitchfork and is being followed with a series of special live performances in varying formations.

Max is a founding member of experimental rock collective JOBS, Amirtha Kidambi's Elder Ones, and several others. He has toured, performed, and recorded with many diverse artists including Wild Up, Steph Richards, Nels Cline, Ava Mendoza, Cass McCombs, DARKSIDE, Normal Love, Jeff Parker, Vinny Golia, Peter Evans, and many others.

Burden of Dreams is the latest band from Oakland composer and multi-instrumentalist, Nathan Clevenger. Along with Clevenger on electric bass, the ensemble features Brett Carson (Hammond organ), Mark Pascucci-Clifford (vibraphone), and Jason Levis (drums). The band's music is dark and dense, drawing from 20th Century classical, doom rock, and jazz.

Photo by Alex De La Hidalga.

events.title: Raptor Fest at Rancho San Vicente
events.description:
Get up close with birds of prey at Raptor Fest, a free educational event from POST and Santa Clara County Parks.

Held at Rancho San Vicente, a POST-protected addition to Calero County Park that is becoming a premier raptor viewing destination in the Bay Area.

What to expect:
- Master Falconer Kenny Elvin of Full Circle Falconry shares the history of falconry, raptor biology and behavior (flight demonstration possible, depending on conditions)

- Booths from local conservation groups including Santa Clara Valley Bird Alliance, San Francisco Bay - Bird Observatory, Wildlife Education & Rehabilitation Center and Predatory Bird Research Group at UC Santa Cruz

- Learn how research, habitat restoration and community action protect wildlife

Choose one show (the presentation repeats):
10:00 to 11:15 a.m.
12:30 to 1:45 p.m.

Good to know:
- Free shuttle required due to limited parking
- Ground seating: bring a picnic blanket (chairs allowed behind blanket seating)
- No pets please (service dogs welcome)
- 75-minute sit-and-listen program, best for kids 10 and older
- Bring a reusable water bottle and dress in layers. No meat products, please
- Event may be canceled for inclement weather
- Please stay home if you have COVID-19 symptoms

Questions or accommodation needs: events@openspacetrust.org

events.title: The Searchers
events.description:
A favorite film of some of the world's greatest filmmakers, including Martin Scorsese and Steven Spielberg, THE SEARCHERS has earned its place in the legacy of great American films for a variety of reasons. Perhaps most notably, it's the definitive role for John Wayne as an icon of the classic Western – the hero (or antihero) who must stand alone according to the unwritten code of the West.

As with many of Ford's classic Westerns, THE SEARCHERS must contend with revisionism in its stereotypical treatment of "savage" Native Americans, and the film's visual beauty (the final shot is one of the great images in all of Western culture) is compromised by some uneven performances and stilted dialogue. Still, this is undeniably one of the greatest Westerns ever made.

The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival returns to the Bay Area to celebrate locally-made cinematic mayhem!

Founded by Peaches Christ & Vinsantos in 2003 at the Bridge Theatre, partially as a showcase for their own short films that weren’t getting traction at “legitimate” festivals, the SFUSFF ran under their care for six years until 2008. After Vinsantos moved to New Orleans, Peaches and fellow film programmer Sam Sharkland wanted to see the fest continue and so revived it in 2011 at the Victoria Theatre where it ran until 2015. Now, after 10 years, the festival has found a new home at the 4 Star Theater under the care of Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X, the maniacal minds behind Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse.

The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival exists to celebrate local, independent filmmaking. We proudly champion the overlooked and underrated, the avant-garde and the alternative, the outrageous, the oddball, and the outlandish. events.title: “Abiogenesis” Opening Reception - new works by Philip Beesley & Casey Curran
events.description:
Heron Arts is pleased to announce Abiogenesis, a duo exhibition featuring Philip Beesley and Casey Curran. The opening reception for Abiogenesis is Saturday, November 14th, 2026 from 6-9pm. It is free and open to the public and will be part of San Francisco Art Week. The exhibition will be on view to the public until January 24th, by appointment only.

Abiogenesis brings together the work of Philip Beesley and Casey Curran around an elusive phenomenon: the emergence of life from inert matter. Their work assembles unmistakably artificial elements that, in their cellular forms and gentle movement, begin to suggest life. Lacework becomes membrane. Scaffolds of repeating cells become skeletons of organisms. Glowing, shimmering light evokes the pulses of nature. Mechanical gestures appear to breathe, bloom, and reach into the world.
Intimations of life within Beesley’s and Curran’s sculptures suggest that living form can emerge from the matter of the earth. Beesley and Curran probe this threshold through myth, science, and sensitive sculptural expression.

Artist Bios

Philip Beesley is a Canadian artist whose sculptures explore the threshold between inert matter and living form. At the heart of his work are glowing, pulsing, precious structures composed of innumerable finely crafted elements. Classically trained in fine art and architecture, he creates immersive installations of lace-like scaffolds and suspended membranes, inviting intimate encounters with light, texture, and gen...

This new album follows on the surprise underground success of their debut: The Head Hurts But The Heart Knows The Truth (released 31 May 2023) releasing on Vegyn’s own PLZ Make It Ruins label.

The debut record has streamed over 19.4 million times on Spotify alone and sold over 8,000 physical copies worldwide. The debut gained its popularity entirely organically with zero marketing or PR spend. Since its release, Headache has built a dedicated global fanbase, with several fans even going so far as to get lyrics or the project’s logo tattooed on themselves.

Thank You For Almost Everything continues the original’s distinct style of Trip-Hop / Downtempo Electronica but combining with its own unique (and now imitated) AI-voiced spoken word. For this new album, Headache steps away from the hum-drum of Blighty and instead focuses his gaze to sunnier shores. Recalling personal histories of ruffled hair and school cafeterias, ancient unsolved Albionic riddles, Rome’s changing seasons and its poignant graffiti, arguments with girlfriends at luxury hotel beachfront restaurants, and what it truly feels like to be alive in this inscrutable but beautiful world.

A path that along the way has seen him release two Top-10 Albums (2017’s ‘Migration’ and 2022’s ‘Fragments, which both landed at #5 on the UK chart), plus numerous Gold and Silver certified singles, sell over 900,000 records, rack up billions of streams, collaborate with the likes of Erykah Badu and Damon Albarn, and be both BRIT and GRAMMY-nominated – the latter seven times, with five in the dance/electronic categories, a record number of nominations shared with The Chemical Brothers, Skrillex and Madonna.

His renowned live show – built around a full live-band, guest vocalists and immersive visuals – has also set the blueprint for how and where an electronic musician can translate their records into the live arena. He has performed to millions of people across the globe, with sold-out shows at prestigious venues like the Sydney Opera House, Alexandra Palace and Red Rocks Amphitheatre – in many cases as one of the first electronic artists to do so – and the world’s biggest festival stages including Glastonbury, Coachella, Sonar and Fuji Rock. Taught to sing by his grandfather in a Church of Christ, Cauthen hit the scene with the duo Sons of Fathers in 2009, before My Gospel, Room 41, Country Coming Down, and Black on Black unveiled a vulnerable, fire-and-brimstone songwriter with brazen Texas attitude – craving deliverance, yet possessed by a “bird dog” instinct for theatrical rapture. Kristal Sotomayor, United States, 2025

A curious trans mermaid defies her mother’s warnings to venture up to the surface, only to discover the world above is not what she dreamt. Las Cosas Que Brillan explores the impacts of environmental destruction, and the danger of being desired in a postcolonial world.

Motherhood (12:22min)

Ava Corder, United States, 2025

Nicki is one of the first trans women to carry a baby to term as part of a groundbreaking uterine transplant trial. Just hours before her scheduled C-section, her water breaks—something the doctors said couldn’t happen. Her physician urges her to stick to protocol, warning that the outcome of her birth could impact access for future trans patients. Her husband, Benny, and her father, Al, beg her to comply. But Nicki chooses to follow her instinct and pursue a natural birth at home. She’ll give birth on her terms.

Long Away (16:32min)

Tilly Bridges & Susan Bridges, United States, 2025

Set twenty-five years into the future, Long Away is a sci-fi story about Victoria and the father who died when she was very young. As a trans woman who transitioned as an adult, Victoria’s father never got to know her truth. She uses a one-round-trip-only time travel device to jump back to our present and meet the man she can barely remember… and try to find out...

events.title: San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival 2026: Third Program
events.description:
The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival returns to the Bay Area to celebrate locally-made cinematic mayhem!

Founded by Peaches Christ & Vinsantos in 2003 at the Bridge Theatre, partially as a showcase for their own short films that weren’t getting traction at “legitimate” festivals, the SFUSFF ran under their care for six years until 2008. After Vinsantos moved to New Orleans, Peaches and fellow film programmer Sam Sharkland wanted to see the fest continue and so revived it in 2011 at the Victoria Theatre where it ran until 2015. Now, after 10 years, the festival has found a new home at the 4 Star Theater under the care of Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X, the maniacal minds behind Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse.

The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival exists to celebrate local, independent filmmaking. We proudly champion the overlooked and underrated, the avant-garde and the alternative, the outrageous, the oddball, and the outlandish. We'll be presenting the silly, subversive, surreal, and strange from all Bay Area filmmakers! From bizarro B-films to midnight movie trash, expect the weirdest and wildest the Bay has to offer, with the night kicking off with our lighter fare and getting darker and more freaky as the evening goes on. Cinematic weirdos - you have found the festival for you!

events.title: Minnette Lehmann Memorial Celebration
events.description:
Doors 12pm / Program 1pm / Open Mic 2pm

RSVP Here (& register for streaming link)

The Bay Area art community mourns the loss of Minnette Lehmann, feminist artist, intellectual, educator, mother, grandmother, wife, and friend to many, who passed away in June, just shy of her 98th birthday. Minnette was one of the longest-serving board members of The Lab, serving for nearly 20 years.

Please gather with us for a memorial and celebration of Minnette’s extraordinary life, art, sharp wit, dry humor, and indelible legacy. The program will be Emcee’d by Kathy Brew with music by Richard Marriott. Everyone is welcome. (RSVP for a remote online streaming option.)

About Minnette

Since the 1940s, Lehmann was at the forefront of important Bay Area intellectual and artistic movements. She hosted countless artists, thinkers, and art-world gatherings at her San Francisco home and enchanting garden overlooking the Bay.

An embodiment of the “wild woman” archetype, she challenged and redefined domestic and artistic institutions for women, expanding possibilities through photography, performance art, collage, and painting. Her groundbreaking photographic series Trouble in Paradise documented a pivotal moment in American history when marriage itself became problematic. She received a National Endowment for the Arts grant for the work.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: Japanese American Legacies of Resistance
events.description:
This Sunday, we are stepping into the historical legacy that inspired OMCA’s latest special exhibition, BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration. With opening remarks by OMCA Executive Director Lori Fogarty, we will engage with this present moment in American history with the clarity and learnings of the past.

Guest speakers Satsuki Ina and Miya Sommers, who both have personal or familial ties to wartime incarceration, will be joined in conversation by host Joemy Ito-Gates to explore how the shadows of this history led them to paths of anti-imperialist organizing, solidarity anchored in love, and healing work in times of enduring racial injustice. TaikoPeace will close the day with an interactive performance of “Ei Ja Nai Ka,” honoring Japanese American immigrant ancestors of this era and the echoes of their resistance through taiko, dance, and song. Come ready to learn, engage, and connect with one another!

Visitors are invited to continue the conversation during a post-program Call to Action gathering. Japanese American Families for Justice, Nikkei Resisters, and Tsuru for Solidarity will facilitate interactive protest art activities and share resources on how to get involved with current campaigns.

This program is a part of our exhibition programming for BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration, on view through December 27, 2026.

events.title: Paranda Party 3: Jeeti Raho
events.description:
Paranda Party is a queer South Asian cultural celebration built around the paranda, a punjabi hair tassel that is braided into the hair. Now in its third year, this is a night where South Asian culture and queerness share the same room.

This year's theme, Jeeti Raho, takes its name from the blessings our elders give us: jeeti raho, khush raho, abad raho. Stay living, stay happy, stay prosperous. Many of us grew up hearing body-shaming comments in the place those blessings should have been. Jeeti Raho reclaims them, on our own terms.

Join us November 7, 2026 at Queer Arts Featured in the Castro for an evening of live performance, original poetry, and paranda tradition brought to life. Expect original music and spoken word from South Asian and queer artists, a close look at the craft of paranda-making, and a collaborative zine filled with community poetry and artwork, available to take home.

Whether you're returning for your third Paranda Party or walking in for the first time, come ready to celebrate, be loud, and be fully yourself.

In the upside-down world of the Addams Family, to be sad is to be happy, to feel pain is to feel joy, and death and suffering are the stuff of their dreams. Nonetheless, this quirky family still must deal with many of the same challenges faced by any other family, especially now that the Addams kids are getting older.

Wednesday Addams, the beloved princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet young man from a seemingly ordinary family. A man her parents have never met. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host dinner for Wednesday’s boyfriend and his parents.

Full of quirky characters, wicked humor, catchy songs, and plenty of heart, this ghoulishly fun musical is a celebration of family, love, and embracing what makes us different.

events.title: Hunting Flies + Roly Poly
events.description:
Presented together, Hunting Flies and Roly Poly are two distinct satirical comedy films by celebrated Director Andrzej Wajda.

Hunting Flies will be preceded by the short film Roly Poly.

Roly Poly – Runtime: 35 minutes

The story of a racing car driver who undergoes so many transplants that it can no longer be determined which people have contributed to his make-up.

Rally driver Richard Fox keeps getting involved in terrible accidents but always manages to survive thanks to organs transplanted from people who died in crashes he caused. The situation complicates when he starts acquiring his donors’ personality traits along with their organs.

Hunting Flies – Runtime: 104 minutes

Wlodek is a shy man who’s afraid of his mother as well as his wife. However, upon meeting Irena, his life takes a new turn.

One of the key films of the Polish film renaissance, this satiric comedy explores the seeming world of emancipated women and emasculated men in Communist Poland. A librarian shares his life and home with his domineering wife. He has an affair with a beautiful intellectual, who wears fly-shaped glasses. She tries to become the woman behind the great artist. It’s a film dedicated to the women of Poland, even as it critiques the relations between the sexes.

Screenings of Andrzej Wajda’s films in the USA in 2026 are part of the ‘Wajda 100 Tour – North America’ project, organized by DI Factory with the financial support of the Polish Film Institute.

events.description:
Goldenvoice Presents
Cry Baby Tour
Vince Staples
Sunday, November 15 | The Warfield

It opens with the ephemeral sounds of nature. Birds, bugs, and airy notes chiming in the air. Then, the undercurrent of something darker, disrupting the fantasy: a distorted voice. “To live is to be,” the voice says, “Like the nigga in the tree.” This is how Dark Times, Vince Staples’ eighth studio album, begins.

It’s a new era in the prolific artist’s canon, a muscular and revelatory work refining elements that have been present in his catalog for the last decade: dense lyricism over lush, layered beats; wry, melancholic observations about life; finding pockets of light in an endless dark. For Staples, the album is “a snapshot” of this period of his life.

“It’s been 10 years since I started putting things out properly,” he says, referencing his first EP, with Def Jam in 2014, Shyne Coldchain Vol 2, “I don’t really keep track of any of that stuff, but it’s important to take a second to appreciate the journey.” The title came intuitively to Staples after he listened to the record in full, noticing heavy motifs that kept reappearing. The album cover, featuring a faintly seen noose, was similarly intuitive.

Staples began recording the album over a seven-month stretch, during weekly sessions in North Hollywood. At the time, he was in post-production on his critically acclaimed Netflix series The Vince Staples Show, which he wrote, produced and starred in. Working on the show was “very, very in...

Todd Day Wait

Todd Day Wait is one of the last real American Workhorse, pedal to the metal, Troubadours by way of Missouri, to California, to New Orleans and now Nashville. The original material of Todd Day Wait, is highly influenced by early American folk, country and blues music from the 1920's through the 1960's, embodying the spirit and authenticity of traditional American music.

Todd Day Wait, whom you may have heard of from his millions of spins on GemsOnVHS or WesternAF writes and performs his own style of timeless country music. Harking back to Jimmie Rodgers, Willie Nelson, Wynn Stewart and Kris Kristofferson he keeps the spirit of country music alive. In 2009 he put all his earthly belongings on the curb and hit the road, in his diesel shuttle bus fueled by vegetable oil, for a never ending tour. Directed by the illustrious William Wyler (The Good Fairy, The Big Country, Ben-Hur), the briskly paced Counsellor at Law is often cited as the best film to ever tackle the intricacies and pitfalls of the legal profession. George Simon (Hollywood legend John Barrymore, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde) is a successful attorney, climbing from a Jewish ghetto to elegant Art Deco offices in the Empire State Building. After allowing one of his former clients to commit perjury to win a case, George realizes he could be disbarred. Flavored with social commentary and wry humor, and featuring a luminous performance by the great Bebe Daniels as George’s secretary Regina, Counsellor at Law is an exceptional example of the hard-boiled dramas that defined the Pre-Code cinema of the early 1930s.

Tuesday, November 17 | Fox Theater

We live in a time when our thumbs know more than our minds. We scroll past each other’s joy and grief before breakfast, absorb a day’s worth of tragedy by lunch, and still convince ourselves that the next notification might be the dopamine hit that’ll make us feel better. As much as some of us complain about smartphones — or, more specifically, what’s on said smartphones — distraction is the air we breathe. Social media, surveillance, endless updates and countless opinions, it all piles up until focus feels like a luxury item. For Thundercat, the clutter isn’t abstract. And on Distracted, his long-awaited fifth studio album, it’s the central theme of his life and art right now.

“If you got an Instagram, you know exactly what I’m talking about,” he says matter-of-factly, half joking, half exhausted, when asked the impetus of the album’s title. Thundercat doesn’t frame distraction as a buzzword or a diagnosis; instead, he treats it like something omnipresent, something you deal with whether you like it or not. Distracted arrives six years after 2020’s It Is What It Is, an album shaped by grief, romantic heartbreak, and the sudden loss of his friend and collaborator Mac Miller. If that record felt like a long exhale after trauma, Distracted feels like the restless pacing that follows: the period when life keeps happening whether you’re ready or not. The inspired collaboration was born of friendship, and mutual admiration, but grew into a synergistic creative partnership that birthed a timeless album of beautifully evocative songs. Unlike anything either artist had done before, the album’s stylistic flourishes include doo-wop, country-rock, baroque pop, folk, and spellbinding torch songs. events.description:
CIIS Public Programs presents renowned mycologist and medical researcher Paul Stamets for an illuminating talk on the history of psilocybin mushrooms exploring their past, present, and future uses. In this presentation, Paul takes you on a journey into the psilocybin mycosphere as he chronicles milestones that further substantiate that psilocybin, and more so psilocybin mushrooms, can help us evolve into the best of what we can be.

The collection and cultivation of psilocybin mushrooms, Paul argues, is central to our practices for freedom of consciousness. Paul shares how psilocybin mushrooms might fundamentally change the many challenges we face as a society. He believes we are at an evolutionary crossroads. Could psilocybin mushrooms help propel us as we emerge into a new version of ourselves, Homo sapiens 3.0?

Paul Stamets, D.Sc. (Honoris causa) is a speaker, author, mycologist, medical researcher, and entrepreneur, who is considered an intellectual and industry leader in fungi. He is the founder and owner of Fungi Perfecti, LLC, and Host Defense Mushrooms supplement line. Paul Stamets is the author of eight books. He named numerous new species of psilocybin mushrooms. In 2023, a new psilocybin mushroom species was named after him to honor his lifelong work: "Psilocybe stametsii." events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Computerwife
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Computerwife

New York City-based Addie Warncke began Computerwife in 2018 at the beginning of her college career, using SoundCloud as a diary to chronicle her emotions. When the pandemic hit, Warncke released the five songs she was proudest of as her self-titled debut EP, and the strength of those tracks led to a signing with Danger Collective Records. Now, she’s poised to release her debut self-titled full-length: a raw and intimate portrait of her experiences processing the small but poignant moments that shape a life. Computerwife’s sound is captivating and nuanced, pushing the boundaries between analog and digital. “The main theme that ties this album together is an interest in the deep web and an attempt to combine existing media to make something new,” she explains. With her seamless blend of shoegaze, emo, and lo-fi noise pop, Computerwife speaks directly to the disquiet experienced by every 21st century digital girl with a tenuous grip on life and identity.

Without any prior production knowledge or a band to work with, expanding her songs beyond the writing stage was a challenge Warncke sought to overcome. A Song Exploder episode about Grimes inspired her to download a free trial of Ableton so she could flesh out tracks and learn more about electronic production. On her dorm room bed, she began to record with her dad’s guitar and bass, a Fender deluxe amp, and a focusrite to Ableton. Her first EP and forthcoming debut LP are pulled from thes...
