Babehoven

Babehoven is the Hudson, NY based project of singer-songwriter Maya Bon and collaborator Ryan Albert. Since 2017, the band has carved out a sound that blends melodic indie and folk rock with an occasional nod towards country. Bon serves as the project’s principal songwriter and lyricist, while Albert, a multi-instrumentalist and producer, further shapes the sonic world around her songs. Together, they’ve built a body of work that feels both intimate and expansive.

"Blue Around You," Babehoven's new single, is a country-flecked stomper. The song finds Bon singing with hard-won resilience: "Yesterday a stranger told me they can see / That I feel levels of pain that could've broken me / And I thought, mmm but I survived it." Recorded at The Chicken Shack and 12 Lb Genius in Upstate NY, Maya and Ryan gathered an excellent crew of musicians with producer Phil Weinrobe at the helm—Oliver Hill, Zosha Warpeha, Dylan Nowik, Jared Samuel, Ellington Peet, and Nick Kinsey. The core of the song was recorded live with no playback or headphones with the feel of the room being as much an instrument as the hardanger fiddle and harmonies that soar overhead.

events.title: Aliens (Special Edition)
events.description:
Where its predecessor was a slow-burn suspenser, Cameron’s ALIENS is a bombastic, no-holds-barred exosuit fight to the finish, an express elevator to hell, goin’ down! Lone survivor Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) goes back for a rematch with the creatures who slaughtered the crew of the Nostromo, this time bringing along a squad of hard-boiled space marines whose number includes the great Bill Paxton, Jenette Goldstein, and Lance Henriksen’s mumblety-peg-playing android Bishop. Rounding out the superb supporting players are the aliens themselves, pinnacles of pre-CGI visual effects that just keep coming, and coming, and coming, and coming… while Mead’s contributions can mostly be seen in the blade-like military vessel Sulaco and the unforgettable “Power Loader” donned by Ripley for the main event grudge match.

Screening in Cameron’s preferred cut, which adds nearly 20 minutes of material not seen in the theatrical version, including glimpses of life at the ill-fated Hadley’s Hope colony and some “kickass” motion-activated turret guns.

“Hot off of the immediate successes of Blade Runner and TRON, Syd Mead was enlisted by Cameron to build out the world of ALIENS, his muscular, action-oriented second chapter to Ridley Scott’s now-iconic 1979 masterpiece. The centerpiece of Mead’s designs is the U.S.S. Sulaco, the military spaceship that transports the Colonial Marines, infusing the vessel with a functional and industrial aesthetic that enhanced the film’s gritty realism.” —Future P...

events.title: Ann M. Evans and Georgeanne Brennan, Market Memories Cookbook
events.description:
Saturday, November 21, 2026, 11:00 am - 11:45 am

Stop by the Foodwise Classroom for a cooking demo featuring the seasonal bounty of the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market.

Georgeanne Brennan is a James Beard and Julia Child award-winning cookbook author. Her association with farmers markets goes back to the 1980s, when her pioneering seed company, Le Marche Seeds, supplied emerging market growers across the country. Her memoir, A Pig in Provence, chronicles her adventures in France, where she still has a home, raising pigs and making goats milk cheese. She lives in Winters, California, with her husband.

Ann M. Evans is a co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and the Davis Food Co-op, and she is a former mayor of Davis, California. A leading proponent of the Farm-to-School movement in California, she worked extensively with former California School Superintendent Delaine Eastin and with Alice Waters on multiple projects. She writes a weekly column for the Davis Enterprise. This is her third cookbook. She lives with her husband in Davis.

They are the co-authors of Market Memories Cookbook: Celebrating 50 Years.

All demos take place in the Foodwise Classroom (green tent in front of the Ferry Building) and are free to the public, with recipes and samples for all.

The demo will be followed by a book signing with book sales courtesy of Book Passage.

events.title: International Bottled Water Tasting Class
events.address: 57 Post Street, Suite 608, San Francisco, CA, 94104
events.description:
Think you can tell Fiji from Evian in a blind tasting? Know your Topo from your Pellegrino just from looking at the bubbles? Have you ever tried salty sparkling Spanish Vichy Catalan, or experienced the bizarre Borjomi from the Republic of Georgia?

Bottled waters differ dramatically in texture, minerality, carbonation, and finish. We’ll try lots of waters - some familiar and some super weird- and we’ll learn Why they taste the way they do in this alcohol-free experience.

We’ll start by blind tasting San Francisco tap to see if Hetch Hetchy is as heavenly as we’ve heard about. We’ll continue blind tasting bottled still waters from neutral to mineral-rich, then crack open a whole bunch of sparkling soda waters and go through them one-by-one.

events.title: Booked & Bottled: Build a Blind Date with a Book
events.description:
Booked & Bottled: Build a Blind Date with a Book

Saturday, November 21, 2:00–5:00 p.m. at Coursey Graves Winery

Taste your way to a book you’ve never read: Coursey Graves pours a flight of wines, each one paired to a genre, and the pour you love points you toward your blind date with a book.

Chardonnay points toward historical fiction, Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir toward romantasy, Syrah toward contemporary fiction, ‘22 Napa Cabernet toward thriller (exact pairings may shift slightly by the day of the event). The books are a curated selection of new releases across all of those genres, so you’ll get a few clues along the way, enough to feel confident you’re walking away with something you’ll genuinely like.

Follow your favorite pour to its genre, then build your blind date: choose from book-themed baubles (bookmarks, stickers, tea, and more) to tuck inside, wrap it all up yourself, and add a pairing card explaining why that book and that wine belong together. The book itself stays a mystery until you’re home and ready to unwrap it.

Your ticket includes a full glass of wine plus your flight of pours, food from Coursey Graves, your wrapped blind-date book and baubles to take home, fun bookish games, and a spot at the book swap. Add-on blind dates are available if you want to build a second one! One bookish blind date is good, but it also makes a great holiday gift for someone else on your list.

events.title: “Castro on Fire”: A Queer Resistance Walking Tour by Unspeakable Vice
events.description:
LOCATION

GLBT Historical Society Museum

4127 18th Street

San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION

$35; Museum admission included in tour

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

Details

Duration: about 90 minutes, plus the round afterward

Meet: GLBT Historical Society, 4127 18th Street

Ends: the Lookout, 3600 16th St at Market

Terrain: city sidewalks with one moderate hill; the Lookout is upstairs, stairs only

Ages: 21+ (free round, one per guest)

Heavy Rain: tours reschedule; your ticket transfers

Full route teasers, the people you'll meet, and sources: unspeakablevice.tour...

events.title: Lucy Kaplansky
events.description:
She started out singing in Chicago folk music clubs as a teenager. Then, barely out of high school, Lucy Kaplansky took off for New York City. There she found a fertile community of songwriters and performers—Suzanne Vega, Steve Forbert, The Roches, and others. With a beautiful flair for harmony, Lucy was everyone’s favorite singing partner, but most often she found herself singing as a duo with Shawn Colvin. People envisioned big things for them; in fact, The New York Times said it was “easy to predict stardom for her.” But then Lucy dropped it all.

Convinced that her calling was in another direction, Lucy left the musical fast track to pursue a doctorate in clinical psychology. Upon completing her degree, Dr. Kaplansky took a job at a New York hospital working with chronically mentally ill adults, and also started a private practice. Yet she continued to sing. Lucy was often pulled back into the studio by her friends, (who now had contracts with record labels) wanting her to sing on their albums. She harmonized on Colvin’s Grammy-winning "Steady On," and on Nanci Griffith’s "Lone Star State of Mind" and "Little Love Affairs." She also landed soundtrack credits, singing with Suzanne Vega on "Pretty in Pink" and with Griffith on "The Firm," and several commercial credits as well—including “The Heartbeat of America” for Chevrolet.

Then Shawn Colvin—who was itching to produce a record—hooked up with Lucy, her ex-singing partner. They went into the studio, and when Lucy’s solo...

events.title: Pearl
events.description:
The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves.

PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

events.title: Point Blank (1967)
events.description:
British director John Boorman brought a European sensibility to a Los Angeles neo-noir: POINT BLANK is Antonioni plus violence, Francesco Rosi without politics. The title reverberates like a pun-point: blank. Lee Marvin is Walker, left for dead in an Alcatraz heist and now out to find the $93,000 he has coming. No more, no less, unless you count revenge. The trail leads to the City of Angels and the syndicate that runs it out of car lots and Santa Monica penthouses, the kind of places you know exist only with a little larceny. Picking up on the modern surface of his locale, Boorman takes a champagne-blonde color scheme to a hallucinatory degree, blonde on blond, like Angie Dickinson's bouffant and Marvin's silvery pate (here, we have the bad, the brunette, and the bald). Los Angeles is inherently horizontal. The payoff, visually and narratively, occurs in that storm drain affectionately known as the L.A. River, viewed from a bridge over imagined waters. (BAMPFA)

events.description: On June 29, 2026, Beijing singer-songwriter Song Dongye released Take Another Moment, his second album and his first full-length release in thirteen years. On this world tour, the new songs will be presented alongside the old favorites that have stayed with listeners all these years. Between 2017 and 2018, Song Dongye released three pivotal singles—“Empty Harbor Song,” “Guo Yuan Chao,” and “To Know”—each quietly expanding the boundaries of folk music and reshaping the industry’s perception of him. Now, thirteen years after his landmark debut Anhe Bridge North, arrives his long-awaited second album, Take Another Moment. Entirely self-conceived, arranged, and produced, it stands as a work that, even now, surpasses all expectations upon listening. Over the years, he has lost weight. He fishes. He takes photographs. He plays with beads. And he has completed Take Another Moment, an album astonishing in both its lyrical scope and sonic depth. He remains the songwriter, arranger, and producer at the center of his work. Alongside him are more than twenty instruments and sound sources, leading lights of China’s jazz world such as Wen Zhiyong, Xia Jia, and Nathaniel Gao, and independent spirits as subtle and reclusive as Xing Jiangbo He is still occasionally playful, perhaps as a way of balancing his absolute seriousness and devotion to music—once even letting his cat's backside appear on an album cover. Released at a time when crime cinema was growing increasingly perverse with the likes of ANGEL HEART (1987), BLUE VELVET (1986), and BODY DOUBLE (1984), Greenaway's film out-shocks the buch by intertwining two of human nature's favorite pastimes: food and sex. Like Marco Ferreri's LA GRAND BOUFFE (1973) and Paul Bartel's EATING RAOUL (1982) before it, food and sex quickly turn into a recipe for something decidedly more sinister and... cannibalistic. events.description:
In a castle in the San Fernando Valley lies the lair of music icon Gary Numan. Outside is an enormous statue of a dragon, inside a St Bernard (almost as large) greets you on arrival. He's a new addition to the family – a rescue pup, and huge. The lord of this manor could be as outwardly intimidating as this entire set-up, but he's a humble presence. Notorious for hits such as 'Are 'Friends' Electric?' and 'Cars', Numan's early career was too often misconstrued, tainted by a sometimes fraught relationship with the media and challenged by the hostility of the music industry at the time, still deeply committed as it was to the guitar, bass, drums approach of old. Numan, however, stuck to his guns, outlasted his naysayers, and became renowned not just as a pioneer but as an institution. Today, with a career that has spanned nearly four decades, his approach to electronic music remains an inspiration to artists across genres and eras, from stadium goliaths such as Depeche Mode, Prince and Nine Inch Nails to alternative heroes such as Beck, Damon Albarn and Marilyn Manson. Even Kanye West owes him a debt and David Bowie once credited him with ‘writing two of the finest songs’ in British music. events.description:
The Wrecks are nothing if not resourceful.

The group’s very origin story is a testament to a rare level of D.I.Y. craftiness that has quietly cemented them as an independent phenomenon with an intensely faithful fan base, over a quarter-of-a-billion streams, and successive sold-out headline tours.

Rewinding back to the beginning, the Los Angeles-based band— Nick Anderson [vocals, guitar, keyboard, production], Nicholas “Schmizz” Schmidt [lead guitar], Aaron Kelley [bass], and William “Billy” Nally [drums]—actually recorded their first batch of tunes under clandestine cover in a “borrowed studio.”

Leaving a small town in New York, Nick had just moved to Los Angeles with a handful of songs. He wound up teaching them to his new bandmates and recording them in the evening at a professional studio in the backyard of a home where his friend was house-sitting.

Everything went according to plan until the last night

“We worked from 5pm until 9am for three days,” he recalls. “On the final day, the girl called us and said, ‘You’ve got to get out of there. The owner is on the way’. We cleaned up, grabbed our gear, and left. As we were pulling out, this woman pulled into the driveway. However, we forgot to dump our work onto an external,” he laughs. “Our buddy snuck back in at 2am, stayed in the dark, and transferred the songs. When he got home, he threw his fist in the air with the external! That really started our process of learning how to be a band and producers.”

The Music of Hey Arnold! Live featuring Jim Lang & The PS 118 AllStars celebrates the 30th anniversary of one of television’s most cherished animated series.

Led by award winning composer Jim Lang, best known for his unforgettable theme music, original songs, and score for Hey Arnold!, this one of a kind concert brings the music of the series to life on stage. Blending jazz, hip hop, blues, R&B and funk, Lang created a sound unlike anything else on television, helping give Hey Arnold! its heart, warmth, humor and soul. Thirty years later, the music continues to connect with fans of all ages and inspire musicians around the world.

Performed by Jim Lang and The PS 118 AllStars, the evening features the show’s unforgettable themes, fan favorite songs, and some of the moments that made Hey Arnold! so special. Accompanied by multimedia visuals and stories from behind the music, the performance also includes a special guest appearance by series creator Craig Bartlett.

Whether you grew up with Hey Arnold! or are discovering its music for the first time, this 30th anniversary celebration is a chance to experience one of animation’s most distinctive and enduring scores performed live by the composer who created it.

events.title: The Room Returns
events.description: What happens when great actors collide with the worst script ever written? Tommy Wiseau's original THE ROOM (2003) infamously burned through $6 million and months of shooting with no-name actors. This reimagining flips the myth on its head. Filmed in under 12 hours, on virtually no budget, with Bob Odenkirk (Better Call Saul), Bella Heathcote (THE NEON DEMON), executive producer Mike Flanagan (The Haunting of Hill House), and directed by newcomer Brando Crawford. With no rehearsal and only teleprompters to guide them, the cast embraced the chaos with Shakespearean gravity, transforming cinematic disaster into unpredictable spectacle – all for charity.

Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.
November 27–December 20, 2026, at Marin Shakespeare Company’s Downtown Theatre, 514 Fourth Street, San Rafael. Friday and Saturday evenings at 7:30 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2 p.m. Additional performances: December 4 and 11 at 11 a.m. (Student Matinees), and December 17 at 7:30 p.m.

events.title: Amtrac
events.description:
Long established for his chameleonic proficiency, Amtrac spent the last decade proving himself with melodic house tracks, infectious indie dance hooks and everything in between. Amtrac is a multi-instrumentalist, vocalist, producer, and DJ. He’s played sold-out arena shows, underground clubs and festivals around the world. His recent co-headline tour with Tourist sold out venues across North America.

He’s released three full-length albums and a slew of varied singles and EPs, not to mention marquee collaborations with Diplo and Leon Bridges, Elderbrook, Shakka and Kaskade. He’s remixed everyone from Bob Moses to Alesso, Two Door Cinema Club, Ellie Goulding, Washed Out, UNKLE, Axwell/Ingrosso, ZHU, Bob Moses & more. He runs his own label, Openers, named in a nod to the way he’s managed to straddle both the bright lights of the mainstage world and the taste-making underground without ever losing sense of who he really is—and still, he’s never felt quite as focused as this.

After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.

events.title: Tower of Power
events.venue: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
events.address: 50 Mark West Springs Road, Santa Rosa, CA, 95403
events.description:
For 58 years, Tower of Power has delivered the best in funk and soul music. East Bay Grease defined their sound and landed them with Warner Brothers. Bump City, their 1972 debut for the label, was a hit on both the Billboard 200 and the R&B Albums. The 70s were a boom period with radio classics like “So Very Hard to Go” and “What Is Hip,” and the band continued to tour and record over the years. Fifty years later, in 2018, they returned to Oakland to celebrate their landmark 50th anniversary. Tower’s window-rattling grooves and raucous party spirit had been a balm for the soul throughout their half-century existence.

The band has traveled the world, enjoying hit singles on their own and backing legendary artists, including Otis Redding, Elton John, Santana, the Grateful Dead, John Lee Hooker, Aerosmith, Bonnie Raitt, and countless others. In the process they’ve defined an “Oakland soul” sound as instantly recognizable as those from Castillo’s hometown, Detroit, as well as inspirations like Memphis and Philadelphia.

events.title: New People: An Eye for an Eye
events.description:
This screening will take place at NEW PEOPLE CINEMA, located at 1746 Post Street in Japantown.

Director Tanaz Eshaghian in person for a post-screening Q&A

An Eye for an Eye unfolds like a real-life courtroom thriller, with stakes as high as life and death. Years after killing her abusive husband in an act of self-defense, Tahereh now faces execution unless she can pay the Diya—blood money demanded by her abuser’s family. With the clock ticking and public sympathy running low, her son Mohsen is thrust into a desperate race against time to save his mother’s life, turning to outside donors in a society where victims of domestic abuse are often met with silence—or scorn. With unprecedented access to private negotiations, legal proceedings, and intimate family moments, the filmmakers bring us deep inside a harrowing moral and legal labyrinth. We witness not only the emotional toll on Tahereh and her children, but also the chilling mechanics of a justice system shaped by patriarchal values and religious law. Gripping and deeply human, An Eye for an Eye lays bare the personal costs of systemic injustice—and the fierce resilience of a family fighting for their right to move forward.

Dweezil Zappa was born on September 5, 1969, in Los Angeles, the son of the iconic musician Frank Zappa. Over the past three decades, Dweezil has carved out an eclectic and illustrious career that spans music, television, film, and entrepreneurship.

A Grammy-winning guitarist, Dweezil has left an indelible mark on the music industry with over 2000 concerts performed worldwide. Known for his masterful performances and deep connection to his father’s music. Dweezil is returning to concert stages in 2026, continuing to guide fans through the thrilling and sophisticated world of his father’s music. His aptly named “DZ 20: Like Father, Like Son” Tour returns to North America in 2026 with shows in major cities across the US and Canada – celebrating 20 years of performing his father’s music.

His virtuosity on the guitar is matched only by his prolific compositional skills, which have generated numerous original works spanning multiple albums including “Confessions of Deprived Youth” (1991) and “Via Zammata” (2015). Notably, his compositions have even been performed by a 100-piece orchestra in Holland, showcasing his versatility and command of orchestral arrangements. His music effortlessly traverses genres, seamlessly weaving together elements of rock, fusion, and experimental sounds, all while maintaining a signature style that is unmistakably his own. events.title: Small Town Gay Bar
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
20th Anniversary
Small Town Gay Bar
Hosted by Peaches Christ w/ special guest Director Malcolm Ingram
Tuesday, December 1 | The Castro

Two decades ago, director Malcolm Ingram shined a beautiful, raw, and deeply moving spotlight on the resilience of LGBTQ+ communities in the Deep South with his groundbreaking documentary, Small Town Gay Bar. This year, we are bringing it back to San Francisco’s most iconic silver screen.

Small Town Gay Bar is a tribute to the resiliency of gays living in rural areas throughout America. A moving portrait of men and women fighting to create and maintain community for themselves in the face of great opposition, hypocrisy and prejudice in a largely ignored subculture of discreet backdoor entrances and hushed sexual expression in small town Mississippi.

Experience the film like never before with a gorgeous, brand-new 4K restoration print that captures every ounce of heart, struggle, and triumph in crystal-clear definition. Following the screening, Peaches will sit down with special guest director Malcolm Ingram for an exclusive, live Q&A diving deep into the legacy of the film, behind-the-scenes secrets, and how the landscape of queer safe spaces has evolved over the last twenty years.

Don’t miss this rare opportunity to celebrate queer history, cinema, and community at the Castro Theatre!

events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents

A Janus Films and Criterion Release
Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
Directed by Paul Thomas Anderson
Presented in 35mm

Wednesday, December 2 | The Castro

Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie.

Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele).

GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a “a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

| Performances: December 2-3, 2026 |

A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set.

Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City.

Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season.

events.description:
Don’t think ELF is one of the best holiday films ever? You sit on a throne of lies!

Christmas movies come and go, but few join the pantheon of the greats. You know the ones – A CHRISTMAS STORY, IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE, and MIRACLE ON 34TH STREET. These are just a few that are invited to sit at the adult table of holiday movies. While the last couple of decades have been pretty sparse when it comes to quality Christmas movies, ELF, the 2003 Will Ferrell comedy, undoubtedly has taken a corner seat at this proverbial table of fame.

Directed by Jon Favreau, ELF is one of those Christmas movies that's impossible to not love It's funny in all the right places, highly quotable, and surprisingly tender. It's Will Ferrell at his Ferrellist.

Don't miss a full night of pointy-toed, jingle bell bliss – especially if you need a pick-me-up in the holiday cheer department – because attending ELF is the Christmas spirit equivalent of putting syrup on your spaghetti.

Jeremiah Chiu is a synthesist in the broadest sense of the word—a craftsperson of the modular synth and other musical instruments and tools, as well as an artist, designer, and educator whose work continually brings disparate forms of knowledge into new relationships. While widely recognized for his versatile electronic music as a solo artist, textured recordings in a duo with violist Marta Sofia Honer, and the experimental quintet he co-leads, SML, Chiu has simultaneously maintained a practice as a graphic designer and visual artist, developing a practice attentive to both the structure of technological systems and the contingencies of liveness and emergence.

For Chiu, visual thinking and musical thinking are not separate disciplines but different expressions of the same innate compositional sensibility. This point of view is born equally from his idiosyncratic sense of aesthetics and his capacity for a warm and porous exchange within a thriving community of creative collaborators that stretches between Chicago and Los Angeles.

Rooted in Chicago's deeply interconnected experimental music community, his music has consistently developed through long-term collaborations and shared artistic inquiry. Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.

Tycho, nitemoves
events.description:
As Tycho, Scott Hansen blends swirling melodies into vaguely triumphant arcs that crisscross between stuttering beats and vocal samples, creating rolling sonic landscapes that extend into the horizon. The San Francisco based Hansen began releasing music in the early 2000’s with The Science of Patterns EP. His first full-length, Sunrise Projector, came out in 2004, and the critical acclaim continued in 2006 with the release of Past Is Prologue. In 2011 with the addition of collaborator and guitarist Zac Brown, Hansen’s meticulous process saw the release of Dive, the first record in a trilogy that was followed by Awake in 2014 and the GRAMMY-Nominated Epoch in 2016, two albums that featured Rory O’Connor on drums. Hansen expanded the scope of his project with the addition of vocalist Saint Sinner on 2019’s Weather, Tycho’s second GRAMMY nomination for Best Dance/Electronic Album. That release was quickly followed by its instrumental companion record Simulcast, a collaboration with alt-R&B artist rum.gold and the Weather Remixes project all in 2020. Another Planet Entertainment Presents
it’s murph

it’s murph is a Nashville-based electronic producer crafting dance music that’s meant to be felt as much as it’s heard. Rooted in emotion but built for movement, his sound lives at the intersection of euphoric melody, gritty low-end, and expansive atmosphere — pulling listeners into moments that feel both intimate and anthemic.

Driven by the belief that music is a multi-sensory experience, it’s murph creates records designed to unlock something deeper: a memory, a feeling, a shared release on the dancefloor. His productions balance warmth and edge, pairing melodic progressions with driving grooves that keep crowds locked in while leaving space to breathe.

Blending influences from tech house, bass-forward dance, and melodic electronic music, his sound draws inspiration from artists like Fred again.., Cloonee, and Chris Lake, while remaining distinctly his own. Whether in headphones or under strobe lights, it’s murph’s music invites listeners to step outside themselves and fully immerse in the moment.

As his catalog continues to grow, it’s murph is carving out a lane defined by emotional energy, forward-thinking production, and a deep connection to the people on the other side of the speakers.

Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Circle Jerks (stylized as Ciʀcle JƎʀᴋs) are an American hardcore punk band, formed in 1979 in Los Angeles, California. The group was founded by former Black Flag vocalist Keith Morris and Redd Kross guitarist Greg Hetson. To date, Circle Jerks have released six studio albums, one compilation, a live album and a live DVD. Their debut album, Group Sex (1980), is considered a landmark of the hardcore genre.

The band has broken up and re-formed several times, sometimes with different bassists and/or drummers. They disbanded for the first time after the release of their fifth album VI (1987), allowing Hetson to focus on Bad Religion (where he had been a member from 1984 to 2013) full-time. The Circle Jerks first reunited in 1994 and released their sixth and last studio album to date, Oddities, Abnormalities and Curiosities, the following year before separating for the second time. The band reunited for the second time in 2001 and spent the next ten years performing live periodically; this reunion lasted for only one new song, "I'm Gonna Live", which was released on their MySpace profile in 2007. Tensions among its members and failed attempts to record the follow-up to Oddities, Abnormalities and Curiosities resulted in the Circle Jerks breaking up yet again in 2011. However, the band announced in November 2019 that they will reunite in 2020 to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Group Sex with live shows.

Another Planet Entertainment presents
Circle Jerks x Repo Man

Sunday, December 6 | The Castro

Circle Jerks formed in Los Angeles in 1979 and quickly became one of the key bands of the early Southern California punk scene. Their debut album, Group Sex, came out in 1980 and remains one of the essential records of the era. More than 40 years later, Circle Jerks are still doing what they’ve always done—playing loud, fast and unapologetic punk rock.

That same Los Angeles punk scene is at the heart of Alex Cox’s 1984 film Repo Man. The movie follows Otto, a young punk who gets pulled into the bizarre world of car repossession while capturing a very specific version of early ’80s Los Angeles.

The night will start with a Circle Jerks set, followed by a Q&A with director Alex Cox, Keith Morris, and Zander Schloss (Kevin the Nerd and Circle Jerks bassist), then a screening of the cult classic Repo Man.

After delivering electrifying performances at Quebec’s major festivals, including the Festival International de Jazz de Montréal, Angine de Poitrine now sets their sights on the prestigious Trans Musicales in Rennes.

All these facts are strictly reserved to the humanoids: Angine de Poitrine are simply thrilled to play rock ’n’ roll.

events.title: Flaming Creatures: The Films of Jack Smith
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 6:30pm / Screening 7pm

$15 / free or discounted for members

Curated & presented by Bradford Nordeen in association with Dirty Looks, The Lab and San Francisco Cinematheque

This program was initially organized in collaboration between Dirty Looks and LA Filmforum

This screening is dedicated to Agosto Machado (????–2026)—“a lady never tells.”

Jack Smith was an underground visionary in every sense of the word. Jack poured glitter into everything he made: pasty creatures, plastic fantasias and moldy monsters. He was a performance artist, filmmaker, playwright, photographer, socialist, aesthete, installation artist, scene-stealer, writer, interventionist. He built a theater and movie-studio in his rickety loft out of street debris; an intricate and child-like universe, Cinemaroc, was equal parts Baroque and broke. For a contingency of art and theater fags and dolls, Jack, as Charles Ludlam once eloquently put it, “is the daddy of us all.” And quixotically, the fact that he remains a somewhat underground or cult figure, as opposed to canonized creature, attests to his legacy.

Best known as a filmmaker, Jack made wild, indeterminable pictures. Flaming Creatures was his first finished film. Well, in truth, it’s his only finished film, since it ricocheted out of his hands when a trend of underground film raids made his opus a trophy for either side of a decency debate. Seized at the same time as Jean Genet’s Un chant d’amour (1950) and Kenneth Anger’s Scorpio...

events.description:
There is something happening between the mountains and the plains. A stirring in the dust. A song rising from the timber. Out of that landscape of grit and grace comes The Fretliners, a band carrying forward the oldest tradition in American music: telling the truth.

You can call them Colorado’s next great acoustic act. You can point to their Telluride and RockyGrass New Artist wins. You can talk about their musicianship, their harmonies, or their ability to command a room. All of those things are true. But they only tell part of the story.

The Fretliners are carving their own path through American music, drawing from bluegrass, Americana, folk, and rock to create something that feels both familiar and completely their own. Their songs carry the weight of long roads, changing seasons, lost loves, and the quiet hope that keeps people moving forward.

What separates The Fretliners is not just how they play, but what they have to say. Their writing feels rooted in something older than trends. They sing about places that shaped them, people who stayed, memories that linger, and the moments that remind us we are still connected to something real.

There is a kind of honesty in their music that cannot be manufactured. Each note feels lived-in,like old wood worn smooth by generations of hands. Each lyric feels like a conversation around a fire, a story passed down because it still matters.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Storefront Church
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Storefront Church

Storefront Church is the project of Lukas Frank, who's drummed in Phoebe Bridgers' band and appeared on her albums, and the first song of his debut album As We Pass features DIIV frontman Cole Smith, but neither of those affiliations really prepares you for what to expect from As We Pass. It's a 9-song collection that's largely made up of bluesy, gothy, emo-y melancholic songs that sometimes sound like a cross between '90s Cure deep cuts and Nirvana Unplugged. (Lukas also cites Scott Walker as an influence, and you can hear that too.) Most of the album is bare-bones and somber, but Lukas also revs things up for the noise punk of "Faction from Under the Grove," and that fits right in too. With As We Pass, Lukas enters a long, line of depressive singer/songwriters, but even with over half a century of music like this, something about Lukas stands out. He grips you right off the bat with album opener "After the Alphabets" -- the kind of song that can make you drop everything and listen as soon as his voice comes in -- and the album stays that compelling throughout. Even with connections to established artists and the great Sargent House label behind him, this doesn't feel like the smash arrival of a hot new buzz artist; it's the subtle arrival of a songwriter whose songs creep up on you and knock you out when you're least expecting it. Usually, that's even better.

A History Worth Repeating: Songs and Stories from Lucius

Friday, December 11 | The Castro

Rooted in mirrored kinship and a captivating vocal blend, Lucius — the Grammy-nominated indie-pop duo of Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig — are songwriters of rare emotional precision, building one of contemporary music’s most enchanting, harmonic sounds. Their voices, described by the Los Angeles Times as “otherworldly,” move in perfect tandem: two instruments so attuned they read as one. events.description:
Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –
“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”
But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”
Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.
From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.
What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

events.title: Understanding Attachment Trauma & Building Resilience with Mindfulness
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller
We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.
This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.
If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.
Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

events.title: Eyes Wide Shut
events.description:
In IT’S A WONDERFUL LIFE, Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey, at the height of his suicidal despair and panic, imagines a world in which he doesn’t exist. Stanley Kubrick goes one step further in sending Tom Cruise down an odyssey of sexual confusion and paranoia to learn the true meaning of Christmas.

Adapted from the Austrian short story Traumnovelle, Kubrick’s final film peeks us into the privileged world of Dr. Bill Hartford and his wife Alice (Cruise and Nicole Kidman), two well-to-do attractive socialites who, by all accounts, have it made. In a marijuana-fueled argument, Alice reveals thoughts of infidelity that send Bill into an existential panic, leading to an absurdist walkabout through New York that involves – you guessed it – a mysterious sex cult run by a shrouded aristocracy.

Did Kubrick make this to break up Cruise and Kidman’s marriage? How much did he know about mysterious sex trafficking rings? Did Sydney Pollack originate the shirtless-in-suspenders look? Clearly, the film poses more questions than it answers. For certain, EYES WIDE SHUT is a brutally funny sexscapade that puts an ellipses at the end of Kubrick’s storied career – and, most importantly – stands as a crucial text for our modern world. Fidelio!

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

June McDoom

There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own.

She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition.

She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for.

Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive....

events.title: Little Women (2019)
events.description:
Having already once revolutionized the coming-of-age story with her debut LADY BIRD, Greta Gerwig has somehow outdone herself with this gorgeous and thoroughly original rendition of the beloved Louisa May Alcott classic. Bringing her effusive humor, authenticity, and irresistible warmth to the otherwise mannered Civil War-era New England, Gerwig's adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN breathes visceral new life into the March sisters – portraying them as unique, complicated, flawed, and astonishingly human. So human that you will leave the theater wanting to text Jo March and, for several reasons, this will not be a possibility.

You may also find it physically impossible not to chef's kiss at the cast, which is as close to pitch-perfect as it gets. Starring Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, and Eliza Scanlen as Beth, LITTLE WOMEN also features Laura Dern (!), Meryl Streep (!), Bob Odenkirk (!), and Timothée Chalamet as the dashing but lovelorn Laurie (!!!).

Save for a fireworks show, sky-written ode, or Mount Rushmore-type situation, we cannot recommend this rich, heartrending wonder of a film anymore. Its timeless charm is sure to capture the hearts of little women (and men) everywhere.

events.title: Yaelokre
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Yaelokre

Sunday, December 13 | The Castro

If you ever feel as if music has lost its capacity for surprise, the beguiling wonder and infinite creativity of Yaelokre will respark your belief. The Filipino-Icelandic artist – real name Keath Ósk (they/it) – fuses three imaginative strands to their visionary expression: intimate, innocent folk infused with leftfield surrealism and instant pop accessibility; artwork which is intricately detailed and beautifully alluring; and storytelling which brings personal experience and poetry into rich, fable-like narratives. What’s more, all three of these elements are crafted by this one visionary artist.

The scale of the fantastical world they have created is vast, both in terms of narrative and lore. But its essence is relatively simple. The songs are set in the fictional world of Meadowlark and chart the adventures of four masked children who comprise a musical ensemble known at The Lark: Cole Seymour, Clémente Dearworth, Peregrine August, and Kingsley. They perform as representatives of The Harkers, mythical beings who express the fundamental principles of nature, wonder and chaos. What’s more, Yaelokre voices all of the different characters within their universe.

events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Pokey LaFarge
with Cicada Rhythm
Wednesday, December 16 | Bimbo's 365 Club

For two decades, Pokey LaFarge has walked his own effortlessly cool road as an exceptionally iconoclastic troubadour – forthright, genuine, and markedly keen to put it all out there. Rent Money now sees him pushing forward yet again in what can be safely declared his finest collection to date, both as an heartfelt expression of personal experience and as no-nonsense social commentary. With its twanging guitars, plucky rhythms, and undeniably captivating melodies, the album soars and swings, its joyous refrains belying the inescapable undercurrent of constant worry and angst that permeates these troubled times. As always, the Illinois native deftly traverses the genre boundaries, seamlessly integrating the myriad strains of 20th-century American music with a freewheeling command of earnest songcraft, inspired performance, and subversive creativity. Rent Money stands tall as an indisputable high-water mark for Pokey LaFarge – a defining collection from a one-of-a-kind artist of rare ingenuity and uncommon candor, now as ever, determinedly crafting a sure-footed brand of deeply human music all his own.

“People are always going to tell you what they think you should play,” says Pokey LaFarge, “what you should sing about, how you should sound, how you should look, how you should act. And I’ve always just been like, nah. Nope. I’ve just completely gone my own way, and...

Robber Robber

Pinpointing the specific catalyst for an avalanche can be slippery — any combination of classic elements, human interference, or freak accident can trigger disaster — and documenting these precise moments often rests on serendipitous reflexes. On Two Wheels Move the Soul, Robber Robber offer themselves as ignition and capture every sound in the wake. Involuntarily thrust into the throws of rootless nomadism, Robber Robber ringleader Nina Cates collects a series of pressurized vignettes to assemble the Burlington quartet’s thrillingly explosive sophomore album.

Two Wheels Move the Soul was written and recorded throughout the winter of 2024 and 2025, a season of Cates’ life characterized by near-constant upheaval. In January of 2025, Cates (and Robber Robber co-founder) Zack James were displaced from their longtime home at the behest of a landlord’s call to have their building demolished. In a moment’s notice — and amidst a particularly brutal Vermont winter — Cates and James were left to fend for themselves. Luckily, the two were able to tap a deep well of support within their community, finding respite on the couches of Lily Seabird, Greg Freeman, and Thus Love’s Echo Mars. An unused attic provided their longest arrangement.

The personal and economic chaos of living at the mercy of nameless powers-that-be redirected into a hyperfocused attention on Two Wheels Move the Soul. Returning to Little Jamaica Studios — one of the sites for th...

events.description:
Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.
November 27–December 20, 2026, at Marin Shakespeare Company’s Downtown Theatre, 514 Fourth Street, San Rafael. Friday and Saturday evenings at 7:30 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2 p.m. Additional performances: December 4 and 11 at 11 a.m. (Student Matinees), and December 17 at 7:30 p.m.

events.title: Whitney Johnson, Lia Kohl, Macie Stewart + Marguerite Brown
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 8pm / Show 8:30pm

$23 / free or discounted for members

Whitney Johnson, Lia Kohl, and Macie Stewart are a trio who utilize string instruments, voices, and manual tape effect processing to craft compositions from alternately tranquil and disquieting improvised music. The three musicians are individually rooted in deep sound exploration, multi-disciplinary composition, and all manner of cross-genre collaboration. The musical ground covered by their solo practices is correspondingly expansive, and their individual recording and performance credits read as a veritable who’s who, ranging from DIY darlings to household names of experimental avant-garde, electronic, indie rock, and more.

Their influences are vast — dispatched with more playful ease than a trio of string instruments is typically approached with, and just as likely to be found in the cloud-obscured mountains of Donegal, the low-rent cacophony of a Midwestern basement, or the revelatory expanse of the Nurse With Wound list as in the storied halls of the academy. Touchstones and areas of interest aside, the main thing that Johnson, Kohl, and Stewart engage with in BODY SOUND is: listening and reacting.

events.title: Venna
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Venna

Friday, December 8 | The Castro

After two EPs and an illuminating start to his career, Grammy Award-winning saxophonist Venna releases his debut album, MALIK.

For Venna, it’s been a whirlwind of a journey to arrive at this point. He’s spent the better part of three years on the road touring, while coming back to London intermittently. In the spaces he finds himself in as a musician, he’s often the youngest in the room. This period gave him the confidence to embark on this next stage of his career.

“Every experience, every memory, every conversation, anything new, any encounter has influenced how this album sounds. I might like a particular guitar tone from it, and then I bring it into my world. Everything has come and conjured into one place, and it’s beautiful to also hear and see,” Venna says.

Speaking on how he found the words to sing: “Does anyone really have the words to say? I don’t know. I don’t know if I had the words to say. I just conjured words and thoughts and tried to make art out of it.”

Featuring vocals from Jorja Smith, Cari, Leon Thomas, Smino, MIKE, and himself, MALIK is where listeners can get lost and find themselves again. The album also features a long list of musicians including Rocco Palladino, Elijah Fox, AoD, J Warner, Marco Bernardis and longtime collaborator, Yussef Dayes.

MALIK embodies the melting pot of sounds that reflects Venna’s environment. Venna doesn’t want to be rooted in jazz alone; his...

events.title: Florencia Ramirez, The Kitchen Activist
events.description:
Saturday, December 19, 2026, 11:00 am - 11:45 am

Stop by the Foodwise Classroom for a cooking demo featuring the seasonal bounty of the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market.

Florencia Ramirez is the author of The Kitchen Activist: Your Step-by-Step Guide to Creating a Planet Smart Kitchen and Eat Less Water: The Solution to Water Shortages is in the Kitchen. A storyteller at heart and researcher by training, she holds a masters degree in public policy from the University of Chicago. Through writing, research, and lived experience, she explores how the everyday choices we make in our kitchens can become acts of environmental and social change. Her work has been featured on NPR, PBS, KTLA, CBS, KCRWs Good Food, and in the Los Angeles Times. She is the founder and Executive Director of the Pesticide Free Soil Project and the recipient of the Environmental Hero Award and the Gift of Freedom Award in Creative Nonfiction. Married and the mother of three Kitchen Activists, she splits her time between Oxnard, California, and Santa Fe, New Mexico.

All demos take place in the Foodwise Classroom (green tent in front of the Ferry Building) and are free to the public, with recipes and samples for all.

The demo will be followed by a book signing with book sales courtesy of Book Passage

events.description:
Symphony San Jose is delighted to partner again with New Ballet, presenting Tchaikovsky’s timeless masterpiece with choreography by Dalia Rawson.

The San Jose Nutcracker takes place in San Jose at the turn of the last century. This unique production features landmarks of the era, with dazzling new scenic elements including a growing replica of the historic San Jose Light Tower and a skyline of San Jose inspired by the city in 1905. Costumes for the first act were inspired by period dolls from the History San Jose archives and the second act was inspired by our valley in the last century, carpeted in orchard blossoms and known as “The Valley of Heart’s Delight.” Swirling snowflakes, waltzing flowers, and The Sugarplum Fairy will make this holiday ballet a new favorite for the entire family!

Based on the humorous writings of author Jean Shepherd, this beloved holiday movie follows the wintry exploits of youngster Ralphie Parker (Peter Billingsley), who spends most of his time dodging a bully (Zack Ward) and dreaming of his ideal Christmas gift, a “Red Ryder air rifle.” Frequently at odds with his cranky dad (Darren McGavin) but comforted by his doting mother (Melinda Dillon), Ralphie struggles to make it to Christmas Day with his glasses and his hopes intact.

About Floating Features

San Francisco Legacy Businesses Red and White Fleet and The Roxie are partnering to turn the hybrid electric vessel Enhydra into a sailing cinema for a limited run of nighttime film cruises on the Bay. Join us this autumn for a 2-hour twilight cruise and a feature film handpicked by the Roxie. Our electric vessel means no engine noise and a totally unique al fresco movie experience.

events.title: Love Actually In Concert
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.description:
Relive the magic of one of the world’s most beloved festive films in a spectacular live-to-film concert experience.

Love Actually In Concert brings the heart, humor and intertwined stories of Richard Curtis’ iconic Christmas classic to the stage. A live orchestra performs the film’s unforgettable soundtrack – featuring Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You”, Craig Armstrong’s emotionally soaring score, and the timeless “Love Is All Around”, while the movie plays in full on a big screen, creating a deeply immersive holiday event.

Love Actually has become a cultural staple since its release, celebrated for its star-studded cast, endlessly quotable moments and its warm, intertwined portraits of love in all its forms. The film’s composer, Golden Globe, BAFTA and Emmy-winning Craig Armstrong is one of the most influential voices in modern film music, known for Moulin Rouge!, Me Before You, Elizabeth: The Golden Age and more.

Over two decades, Love Actually has built a global multi-generational fanbase, becoming an annual tradition for millions. Its continued popularity is reflected in consistent sell-out screenings, seasonal re-releases and enormous online engagement every December. Audiences return year after year because the film’s emotional honesty, British wit and musical nostalgia strike a universal chord — making this concert experience the ultimate way to start the festive season.

The Warm Me Up Holiday Tour
David Archuleta
Saturday, December 19 | The Castro

Since first stepping into the pop spotlight at age 17, Miami-born singer/songwriter David Archuleta has embodied the kind of genuine star power that can’t be manufactured. After years of dazzling audiences with his radiant personality and phenomenal voice; a journey that’s included turning out multiple platinum-selling hits, achieving global acclaim, and emerging as an undeniable fixture in pop-culture.

As witnessed on his Earthly Delights EP and headlining tour throughout 2025, the collection of works included the worldwide hit single,“Crème Brulée,” that has surpassed over 8 million streams, “Dulce Amore” & “Can I Call You,”David continues to share new sides of himself. He shares, “I’m in my indulgence mode when it comes to giving into my sensuality. Something I always villainized before. There’s something sweet about being naughty. And it’s actually helped me to get in touch with more tender vulnerable parts of myself. So Earthly Delights took in the pleasures of what I always thought would keep me out of heaven.”

events.description:
Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing.

Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu.

Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. events.title: Elvin Bishop
events.address: 417 Alvarado Street, Monterey, CA, Monterey, CA, 93940
events.description:
Ever since Rock & Roll and Blues Hall Of Famer Elvin Bishop first hit the scene with the Paul Butterfield Blues Band back in 1965, he's blazed his own musical trail. Whether he was playing raw, eye-popping blues, or penning the evergreen radio hit Fooled Around And Fell In Love, or touring the world for decades delivering his original, good-time countrified blues, Bishop has always inspired his fans with his rowdy guitar playing and witty, slice-of-life songs. Rolling Stone calls Bishop "a legendary guitarist" whose playing is "impeccable and spirited...a distinguished American player."

Late in 2015, Elvin Bishop formed The Big Fun Trio, with Bishop on guitar and vocals, and his friends Bob Welsh on piano and guitar and Willy Jordan on cajón (a hand-played Peruvian drumbox) and vocals. After playing just a handful of live dates, the group's instantly crowd-pleasing music and undeniable chemistry took the blues world by storm. With the release of their self-titled CD in 2017, media and fan response was immediate and overwhelming. DownBeat celebrated Bishop's "verbal hijinks, outstanding guitar work and country boy friendliness." OffBeat said The Big Fun Trio was "intricate, funky and uplifting," declaring them, "consistently great." With its top-shelf musicianship and front-porch vibe, the album earned a Grammy Award nomination.

The Big Fun Trio quickly discovered the more they played live, the more fun they had making music together. So a follow-up recording was an easy dec...

events.title: My Very First Nutcracker
events.description:
My Very First Nutcracker is a special one-act presentation of The San Jose Nutcracker ideal for families with toddlers, preschoolers, and young children.

This joyful holiday production features the festive holiday party, at which Uncle Nikola reveals his fascinating gifts. Kids will marvel at the historic San Jose Electric Light Tower rising magically above the streets of San Jose, and cheer on adorable mice and toy soldiers who compete to win a magic crown. Introduce your family to the magic of classical ballet!

NOTE: My Very First Nutcracker does not include the second act of The San Jose Nutcracker where Clara meets the Sugarplum Fairy and journeys to the Valley of Heart’s Delight.

For the complete two-act classical ballet visit the main Nutcracker page here.

Children aged one year and older require a ticket for entry.

events.title: The San Jose Nutcracker
events.description:
Symphony San Jose is delighted to partner again with New Ballet, presenting Tchaikovsky’s timeless masterpiece with choreography by Dalia Rawson.

The San Jose Nutcracker takes place in San Jose at the turn of the last century. This unique production features landmarks of the era, with dazzling new scenic elements including a growing replica of the historic San Jose Light Tower and a skyline of San Jose inspired by the city in 1905. Costumes for the first act were inspired by period dolls from the History San Jose archives and the second act was inspired by our valley in the last century, carpeted in orchard blossoms and known as “The Valley of Heart’s Delight.” Swirling snowflakes, waltzing flowers, and The Sugarplum Fairy will make this holiday ballet a new favorite for the entire family!

events.title: Rockin' Holiday at The Henry J.
events.venue: Henry J. Kaiser Center for the Arts, Oakland
events.description:
Celebrate the season with Rockin’ Holiday at The Henry J., a festive afternoon of music, movies, and family fun.

The celebration begins with a lively 30-minute performance by GRAMMY-winning family music group Alphabet Rockers, whose joyful songs invite kids and grown-ups alike to move, sing, and dance together. After a short intermission, settle in for a screening of the beloved holiday classic Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, featuring Rudolph, Hermey the Elf, Yukon Cornelius, and the unforgettable Island of Misfit Toys.

Santa Claus will be on site throughout the event for family photo opportunities, and festive snack bags will be available for advance purchase.

Bring the whole family and make some holiday memories at The Henry J.

Interested in changing, reducing, re-evaluating, or stopping your use of stimulants such as meth or cocaine?

This program is a positive reinforcement 12 week/24-session program with medical services, individual counseling, case management, and support group with all services provided in Spanish.

For more information or to join the group, please contact Maricruz at 415-632-9722 or mmoreno@sfaf.org.

This unique production features landmarks of the era, with dazzling new scenic elements including a growing replica of the historic San Jose Light Tower and a skyline of San Jose inspired by the city in 1905. events.description:
El Grupo de Apoyo Latino de SFAF es un grupo social y educativo que ofrece un espacio abierto, seguro, y confidencial para apoyar a la comunidad Latina afectada por el VIH y SIDA. Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

Every bird holds a memory. Every memory holds a meaning. Across different cultures and communities, across time and space, birds have played a significant role in shaping our understanding of the world, ourselves, and our relationship in nature.
On Sunday, October 18th, this year’s Berkeley Bird Festival invites you to celebrate our incredible birdlife here in the Bay Area through the theme of “Myth and Memories”.
Get outside and witness the birds and our shared environment. Engage with the Myth of the Flying Africans. Fold a crane for peace and longevity. Hear the story of SF’s Wild Parrots. Watch the street “split the sky” through a dance inspired by migration. Listen to the science behind wildlife and remember, every feather, past and present, is a portal to a world where all of us thrive.
This festival brings science, art, and culture under its wing to inspire our collective imagination and action in protecting birds and our environment. We hope you’ll join us whether you’re bird-curious or a long-time advocate.
Register in advance to attend a trip, or gather your flock, swoop in, and dive into a world of birds, Myth and Memory.

Next is “The Dreaming Game,” directed and produced by Jordan Salvatoriello. The film follows 70-year-old Raymond Gaines, a Boston native and lifelong baseball fan, as he returns to Fenway Park after spending 47 years in prison for a murder he did not commit. events.title: MainStage 1: Beethoven’s Eroica, A Hero’s Journey
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSan Francisco Chamber OrchestraProgram:
Ludwig van Beethoven – Coriolan Overture, Op. 62
Grace Williams – Sea Sketches
Ludwig van Beethoven – Symphony No. 3 in Eb Major, Op. 55 “Eroica”

Betrayed by Napoleon’s thirst for power, Beethoven furiously tore apart his 3rd Symphony’s dedication, and in doing so created a work that captured, like no other, the defiant and life-affirming heroic spirit. With its massive size and emotional power, the Eroica Symphony would change the course of Classical music forever.
Our program begins with the Coriolan Overture, Beethoven’s electrifying portrait of Shakespeare’s doomed warrior followed by Grace William’s hauntingly beautiful Sea Sketches, which paint the Welsh coastline in all its wild, shimmering glory.

events.title: Tapas Tuesday – 10% Off all Spanish Tapas at Bota
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerBota Tapas & Paella BarBota Tapas & Paella Bar near Downtown San Francisco and Union Square is doing “Tapas Tuesdays” and enjoy all of our delicious Spanish Tapas at 10% Off. Just mention “Tapas Tuesday” to our server before ordering to get the discount. If you are seeking authentic Spanish cuisine, stop by and say hi!
About Bota Tapas and Paella Bar

As an age-old tradition dating back to the early 1800s, Spanish travelers used “BOTA”, or traditional sheep-skinned repositories, to transport and share their wine. The Spaniards historically thrived on the values of sharing and community: two ideals that have buoyantly withstood the test of time. Tailored around these same ideals are Spain’s cuisine and the development of “tapas,” style dining – where individuals share small plates and memories. From Seville to San Francisco, and across the world, our goal is to initiate more memories – this is why and how we operate. Whether it be with your friends or family, we here at Bota sincerely hope that you enjoy this stop on your journey.

In 2004, Alain Damasio’s Horde of the Counterwind: An Epic Voyage to the Upper Reaches gained acclaim as France’s genre-defining sci-fi odyssey of the 21st century, inspiring the celebrated video game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and igniting the imaginations of millions around the world. Now, this seminal work appears in English translation for the very first time, offering even more readers the opportunity to experience a masterpiece of epic scope and visionary world-building in which twenty-three adventurers climb endlessly against the wind that plagues their desolate homeland. Their only purpose: identifying the mysterious source where eight centuries of past climbers have tried and failed. events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe Invisible Mammal

Award-winning documentary highlights global bat extinction crisis

The Citizens Environmental Council invites you to a free screening of an award-winning documentary highlighting the fight to save North American bats on Wednesday, October 21, from 6 to 8 p.m. at the Burlingame Community Center at 850 Burlingame Ave. in Burlingame. There is no charge for admission, but pre-registration is required. Watch the trailer below!

Just in time for Halloween – and Bat Week! – “The Invisible Mammal” focuses on the plight of several species of North American bats now at risk because of a deadly fungal disease called White-nose Syndrome (WNS) and a team of women biologists determined to rescue these rapidly vanishing species. After a screening of the 90-minute film, filmmaker Kristin Tièche will offer insights and answer questions about a strategy called Operation Fat Bat, pioneered by women scientists, that could rebuild healthy bat populations across North America.
Bats save U.S. agriculture billions of dollars in pesticide use each year, and the decline of bat populations is linked to an increase in infant mortality where these pesticides are used. Since 2006, WNS has decimated bat populations across 42 states and Canada, killing millions of bats.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerProfs and Pints Alameda presents: “Faith and Frights,” a Jesuit priest’s take on religious themes in notoriously terrifying movies, with the Rev. Dennis Recio, S.J., lecturer in English and teacher of a seminar on horror films at the University of San Francisco.
Many have been left praying for salvation from darkness based not on what they had heard in church, but what they had watched in a movie theater. Forget depictions of fictional vampires, werewolves, and zombies. Nothing unsettles quite like a religiously themed horror movie featuring evil forces and evil beings that we might truly believe exist.

Spend an evening confronting the power of religiously themed horror with Father Dennis Recio, a scholar of horror films on the same team as those priests you’ve seen warning of the antichrist, performing exorcisms, or getting hurled by demons out windows and down stairs. He’ll talk about what Hollywood gets right in its depictions of religion in horror films, as well as where it stumbles. He’ll explore why religiously themed horror often generates so much buzz and why it has so much appeal.
He’ll start by describing how horror films are rooted in Gothic literature of the eighteenth century and derived from such literature a focus on the depiction of anxiety during periods of social and religious unrest. events.title: Astronomy Lecture: Living with the Stars on the Day of the Dead (SF’s Randall Museum)
events.description:
Join the San Francisco Amateur Astronomers for this free event. We are thrilled to welcome Dr Isabel Hawkins, Emeritus Exploratorium. As always, come a few minutes early for the best snacks!
Equinoxes and solstices are familiar astronomical markers of the seasons, but the cross-quarter days—the halfway points between them—are less commonly considered in popular culture. At the latitude of some of the oldest Maya cities in Mesoamerica, the cross-quarter day between the September equinox and December solstice coincides with the season of corn harvest and the traditions of Day of the Dead. These traditions reflect a rich intersection of Indigenous astronomy, agricultural cycles, and the enduring practice of honoring and welcoming the ancestors. Solar events, including the zenith and nadir passages of the Sun, as well as the November meridional culmination of the Pleiades, have important cultural and astronomical connections to this season.
A Day of the Dead altar or “ofrenda” will invite audience interaction—we ask interested participants to please bring a personally meaningful belonging, or portrait of a dearly departed, to place on the altar for the duration of the evening and take it home afterward, creating a temporary shared space for remembrance and connection.

Isabel Hawkins, Ph.D., is an astronomer and Emerita at the Exploratorium in San Francisco, whose work bridges science, culture, and public engagement. Born and raised in Córdoba, Argentina, she earned her doctorate...

Riding shotgun is Irena Smith, whose memoir Troika is a modern-day Odyssey set in California’s Central Coast, as three generations of women share profound family stories and create new ones. events.description:

Joined by anthology contributors and world-class masters of the genre Linda D. Addison, Theresa DeLucci, Brian Evenson, and Jeffrey Ford, Datlow will offer a rare peek behind the publishing curtain, introducing the authors reading from their featured works with insights on how each one was hand-picked for inclusion in her anthology. But that’s not all—Datlow will also sit down with Locus Magazine editor-in-chief Liza Trombi to discuss four-plus decades of her legendary career in the horror genre, and the countless authors she’s shepherded to print. Doors at 7:30pm.
